Wider Sports News.title: HSBC Goes Big-Wave Surfing to Make a Splash with ‘The Right Wave’ — LBB - LBB
Wider Sports News.summary: HSBC Goes Big-Wave Surfing to Make a Splash with ‘The Right Wave’ — LBB LBB - Little Black Book
Wider Sports News.body:
HSBC has launched a hero brand film ‘The Right Wave’ to bring to life its role as a trusted banking partner for its customers. The cinematic hero film explores the extreme, high-pressure dynamics between a big-wave surfer, Matahi Drollet and a jet ski driver, Tahurai Henry, as they conquer overwhelming 25ft swells. Drawing on the relationship between Matahi and Tahurai, the film symbolises HSBC’s role in bringing expertise, and deep understanding of the world’s changing currents to build the right conditions for customer success.

The film was shot on Tahiti’s renowned surf break Teahupoʻo during several high-risk wave breaks. Produced by Superprime Films, the team collaborated with local Polynesian production company, We Are Ora to draw on Teahupo’o’s local and specialist knowledge to capture the best possible wave conditions. It was directed by the celebrated filmmaker Kiku Ohe alongside cinematographers Tim Lorentzen and Morgan Maassen.

Wider Sports News.title: SportAccord’s Kelly Fairweather on rebuilding relevance in sport’s new reality
Wider Sports News.summary: Nearly one year after joining SportAccord as managing director from the ITF, Kelly Fairweather discusses the challenges facing federations today and how the upcoming SportAccord Forum has been designed to help navigate them. The post SportAccord’s Kelly Fairweather on rebuilding relevance in sport’s new reality appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
When Kelly Fairweather took over as managing director of SportAccord last year, he arrived having viewed the international sports ecosystem from several vantage points. The South African spent nearly a decade as sports director of the International Olympic Committee (IOC) before a brief stint at the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA), where his remit included overseeing relations with international federations (IFs). Fairweather went on to run two of those IFs, first as chief executive of the International Hockey Federation (IHF), followed by the same role at the International Tennis Federation (ITF).

Having sat both alongside and across the table from IFs, Fairweather has firsthand insight into what those federations need from an event organiser like SportAccord, which has served as a meeting place for the international sports community for more than two decades.

Wider Sports News.title: HSBC extends decade-long Nasdaq Calypso partnership to ETD clearing
Wider Sports News.summary: HSBC extends decade-long Nasdaq Calypso partnership to ETD clearing LeapRate
Wider Sports News.body:
HSBC has adopted Nasdaq Calypso’s enhanced ETD clearing platform, extending a 2011 partnership to unify OTC, ETD, repo and UST clearing under one system. HSBC has expanded its long-running technology partnership with Nasdaq to bring exchange-traded derivatives clearing onto the same platform it has used for OTC clearing since 2011. The bank has adopted Nasdaq Calypso’s enhanced ETD clearing capability, giving it a single, integrated infrastructure spanning OTC derivatives, repo and, by year-end 2026, US Treasury cash transactions.

HSBC’s Derivatives Clearing Services already executes ETD transactions for institutional clients across 40 global futures exchanges, clearing both ETDs and OTC derivatives through the world’s largest central counterparties. Since 2011 the bank has used Nasdaq Calypso to clear clients’ interest rate, inflation and credit default swaps, and it also runs repo clearing on the platform. Extending that relationship to ETDs closes the last major gap in the multi-product setup.

Rugby.title: One-cap England star Charlie Atkinson decides PREM club future
Rugby.summary: Gloucester have confirmed that Charlie Atkinson has signed a new contract that will keep him at Kingsholm until at least 2029.
Rugby.body:
Gloucester have confirmed that Charlie Atkinson has signed a new contract that will keep him at Kingsholm until at least 2029. The 24-year-old fly-half joined the Cherry and Whites in early 2024 and has since established himself as their first choice fly-half, seeing off the challenge of ex-Ireland international Ross Byrne, who was signed in 2025.

Atkinson enjoyed a standout 2025/26 campaign, sweeping Gloucester’s end-of-season awards after being named Coaches’, Players’ and Supporters’ Player of the Season. His form has also been recognised internationally. The former Oxford RFC player has made six England A appearances and earned his first senior England cap against the USA in 2025.

Rugby.title: ‘The gap’s getting bigger’: The changing face of English rugby
Rugby.summary: Six Nations titles, low-scoring games and former rugby league players: three things that have seemingly vanished from men's rugby union in England.
Rugby.body:
Six Nations titles, low-scoring games and former rugby league players: three things that have seemingly vanished from men’s rugby union in England. England’s Six Nations struggles and the Gallagher PREM’s increasingly basketball-like scorelines have been well documented, but the disappearance of rugby league converts has happened far more quietly.

In the 2000s, four former league players represented England in rugby union, with Jason Robinson the poster boy. Seven followed in the 2010s. So far this decade, there have been none.

Rugby.title: ‘The RWC countdown clock is ticking. The permutations are endlessly fascinating. England are in a critical phase.’
Rugby.summary: South Africa are in that good place again, a potential Wallabies resurgence is on the cards but England's form has been variable.
Rugby.body:
England supporters must feel like Butch Cassidy as they look at their team and wonder, “Who are those guys?” Butch eventually did find out when the pursuing posse closed in while Sundance chided his pal in typically laconic fashion: “That’s your trouble. You’re always thinking”.

So, who are Steve Borthwick’s guys – the lot who won 12 matches on the spin not so long ago or the mob who flunked the 2026 Six Nations, thumped by Ireland at home and beaten by Italy for the first time ever? Or even the gallant, up-and-at-‘em outfit that did at least close that dreadfully disappointing championship with a gutsy performance against France?

Rugby.title: Hector Patterson: 'I hear stories about Gary Armstrong
Rugby.summary: Edinburgh's impressive and assertive young scrum-half hails from the Borders heartlands and is primed for a breakout campaign.
Rugby.body:
For 50 blistering minutes, Edinburgh ran Ulster into the Affidea plastic. The ambition and accuracy, the verve and the tempo, and the supreme levels of fitness required to deliver it, had not been seen from this side in an age. Edinburgh scored belter after breathtaking belter, and though they almost succumbed to a very Edinburgh-like capitulation late on, the hope is, victory heralds a new dawn for a club which has lain stagnant far too long.

Watching Edinburgh these past few seasons has typically been as exciting as filling in a tax return. It raised your blood pressure, yes, but probably not your pulse. In one glorious hour, the formulaic, turgid fare of old melted away under the Belfast floodlights.

Rugby.title: Simon Middleton: Why Lesley McKenzie and Shaun Edwards can transform their new teams
Rugby.summary: Ex-Red Roses boss Simon Middleton muses about Lesley McKenzie's move to coach Os Lobos and Shaun Edwards' arrival in England camp.
Rugby.body:
The first thing is that I think Lesley McKenzie is one of the best infielders at her craft, particularly in the contact area or the contact defensive area. This isn’t to say she isn’t very strong in other areas; she is a well-rounded coach, but every coach specialises in one thing. In Lesley McKenzie’s case, that is contact. Personally, I’ve never seen or worked with a better contact coach than her – whether in the women’s or men’s game.

But don’t take my word for it; take Dean Benton’s [former head of sport science for England Rugby and Director of Rugby Melbourne Storm] or Ollie Richards’ [acclaimed S&C coach, specialising in MMA fighting], as they both could attest to the same.

Rugby.title: A comprehensive guide to the 2026 World Rugby Under 20 Challenger Cup
Rugby.summary: 2026 will mark the debut of the newly established World Rugby Under 20 Challenger Cup, with eight nations from all over the world meeting in Chile to fight for a chance to claim the title.
Rugby.body:
2026 will mark the debut of the newly established World Rugby Under 20 Challenger Cup, with eight nations from all over the world meeting in Chile to fight for a chance to claim the title.

Chile will host Portugal, Romania, Hong Kong China, Brazil, Canada, Belgium and Namibia over the next fifteen days, with the competition’s first kick-off set for this Friday. The tournament is split into two groups of four teams: Brazil, Chile, Romania, and Hong Kong China in Group A, and Portugal, Canada, Namibia, and Belgium in Group B. All matches will be played at CARR Parque Mahuida in Santiago, Chile; the first round is scheduled for October 2, the second for October 7, and the third for October 12, followed by the finals on October 17, where each group winner will compete for the chance to be named champions.

Rugby.title: Rugby World Cup 2027 marks one year to go with ticket sales milestone
Rugby.summary: “In just 365 days, Australia will welcome the world for Men’s Rugby World Cup 2027, a landmark tournament that coincides with the competition's 40th anniversary and promises to be the biggest and most accessible celebration of rugby ever staged.
Rugby.body:
It’s officially one year until Rugby’s pinnacle tournament, the Rugby World Cup, with World Rugby celebrating a special ticketing milestone for the tournament, which will be held in Australia between October 1 and 13 November 2027.

1.3 million tickets have already been purchased by supporters from 164 countries, showcasing the global want and anticipation for the eleventh edition of the Rugby World Cup. Out of the tickets purchased with over a year to go until the marquee tournament, 51 per cent of the people are aged between 16 and 44.

Rugby.title: Hunter Paisami learns fate after late yellow card against Springboks
Rugby.summary: "The Disciplinary Committee has found Australian midfielder Hunter Paisami guilty of dangerous play for a contrary tackle, in breach of Law 9.13.
Rugby.body:
The Wallabies will be without powerful Reds No.12 Hunter Paisami for the 2026 Bledisloe Cup series after receiving a six-week ban for a high shot in the 78th minute against the Springboks.

The 28-year-old has been handed a six-game ban but will miss four Test matches, with the disciplinary committee adding a two-game reduction due to his recent disciplinary record and other mitigating factors.

Rugby.body:
The Hurricanes have called upon six-time Super Rugby Pacific champion Bryn Hall to back up Cameron Roigard for the 2027 season, signing the former Crusaders and Blues halfback on a one-year deal.

Rugby.body:

Rugby.title: Leinster and Ireland reportedly dealt Caelan Doris hammerblow
Rugby.summary: Leinster and Ireland have suffered another setback, with captain Caelan Doris expected to remain sidelined until at least the new year after complications have delayed his recovery from surgery, The Irish Times have reported.
Rugby.body:
Leinster and Ireland have suffered another setback, with captain Caelan Doris expected to remain sidelined until at least the new year after complications have delayed his recovery from surgery, The Irish Times have reported.

The No. 8 injured his foot during Leinster’s United Rugby Championship final victory over the Bulls in June and underwent surgery, with a knee procedure also carried out. His rehabilitation has since been slowed by an infection in the knee, pushing his anticipated return beyond the Nations Championship in November.

Rugby.title: Morgan and Lake lead the charge across the Severn Bridge as Welsh influence grows
Rugby.summary: Gloucester's star summer signings inspired their new club to a fantastic 45-24 win over last season's finalists Exeter Chiefs.
Rugby.body:
The Gallagher PREM feels more Welsh than at any point in its 30-season history, even in the two seasons that London Welsh were in the top division in England. Sure, plenty of Welsh players have played in the PREM in the past – the Bath front-row pair, Jon Humphreys and Paul James, used to car share for the commute over the Severn Bridge, while northern clubs Sale and Leeds often looked that way in their recruitment. But not in the same quantity, or quality, as now.

Jac Morgan and Dewi Lake, who’ve captained their country within the past 12 months, were two of the headline acts of the summer transfer activity, swapping Ospreys for Gloucester.

Rugby.title: France forced to find new captain for New Zealand tour
Rugby.summary: France captain Pauline Bourdon Sansus will not travel to New Zealand for her team's WXV Global Series fixtures against the Black Ferns.
Rugby.body:
France captain Pauline Bourdon Sansus will not travel to New Zealand for her team’s WXV Global Series fixtures against the Black Ferns. In agreement with the coaching staff led by François Ratier, the scrum-half will remain in France for family reasons. She remains available to join the squad if required. A new captain will be announced on Wednesday 7 October.

Bourdon Sansus’ absence means France will turn to a new captain for their tour of New Zealand. With regular skipper Manae Feleu unavailable this autumn as she prioritises her medical studies, Ratier will have to select his latest leader carefully.

Rugby.title: Tom Curry extends Sale Sharks contract
Rugby.summary: England international flanker Tom Curry signs a two-year contract extension with Sale Sharks.
Rugby.body:
England international flanker Tom Curry has signed a two-year contract extension with Sale Sharks. The 28-year-old has spent his entire career with the Sharks and made his debut aged 18 in October 2016 and his new deal will keep him with the Prem side until the end of the 2027-28 campaign.

Director of rugby Alex Sanderson said Curry, whose identical twin brother Ben also plays for the club, is "fundamental" to the team. "The terms are a couple of years and that's on Tom's desire to ensure that he's physically in the best spot to be able to honour his contract, to play a load of games for the next two years," Sanderson said.

Rugby.title: Matt Ferguson exits Harlequins to take up Red Roses role
Rugby.summary: Matt Ferguson has left his role with PREM Rugby club Harlequins to take up a role with the RFU as a scrum and contact skills coach.
Rugby.body:
Matt Ferguson has left his role with PREM Rugby club Harlequins to take up a role with the RFU as a scrum and contact skills coach. The former Northampton Saints scrum coach will work with John Mitchell’s Red Roses and in the women’s pathway system. In a previous stint with the RFU, Ferguson was the Red Roses’ forwards coach for three years and contributed to the team’s run to the 2017 Women’s Rugby World Cup final.

Ferguson is credited with converting Sarah Bern from a back-row to tighthead prop. He then spent seven seasons with Northampton Saints between 2018 and 2025, in which time a number of the East Midlanders’ tight five forwards gained Test honours, before he joined Harlequins as lead rugby transition coach.

Rugby.title: Claire Thomas column: The Red Roses are learning to win without winning
Rugby.summary: It’s a cliché - but, these days, you don’t lose: you learn.
Rugby.body:
It’s a cliché – but, these days, you don’t lose: you learn. Defeats are simply an opportunity to get better, and experiences only wasted if they don’t lead to forward motion. If evolution is the outcome, then don’t sweat the process, and it’s no bad thing to snap a win streak if it galvanises the next one. Capiche?

If we’re going with that, then Red Roses – Canada ending in a dead heat was the *perfect* result for the world champions. Their unbeaten run – phew – rumbles on, but 26-26 delivered quite the wake-up call, and forced England to plumb depths which had grown, frankly, dusty.

Rugby.summary: Northampton teenager James Pater rose slow and stealthy as a prospest, but his opening-day Prem hat-trick has blown the full-back's cover.
Rugby.body:
Every other year, towards the end of pre-season, Northampton's players are given a pair of smart shoes. Courtesy of a club sponsor - one of the town's many historic cobblers – each pair is personalised with its new owner's 'Saints number', an individual mark of recognition given to everyone have represented the club's first XV.

James Pater was handed his first set with his number - 2,110 - inscribed on the sole, earlier this month. On Friday, he showed how well he can fill a pair of shoes. With club captain George Furbank having moved to Harlequins, Pater was named at full-back for the Prem opener against Newcastle Red Bulls.

James Pater was handed his first set with his number - 2,110 - inscribed on the sole, earlier this month. On Friday, he showed how well he can fill a pair of shoes. With club captain George Furbank having moved to Harlequins, Pater was named at full-back for the Prem opener against Newcastle Red Bulls.

Rugby.title: Has the balance between attack and defence become too lopsided?
Rugby.summary: There was a record amount of tries on the opening weekend of the Gallagher Prem, but has it got out of hand?
Rugby.body:
Who would want to be a defence coach right now? The opening weekend of the Prem delivered a record 52 tries, the chaotic Australia v South Africa classic in Perth nine more. Rugby union’s ever-evolving balance between attack and defence has never been so strongly weighted in favour of the former.

Whether this is a good thing or not depends on your standpoint. Professional rugby is in the entertainment business and a try is its crowd-on-feet, adrenaline-spike moment. Plenty of tries equals plenty of excitement.

A year to go until the inaugural Lions Women's tour and two of the biggest names in the game are having their first ever face-to-face meeting in a hotel in Shepperton. Rugby.title: Ireland to host England at Aviva Stadium in Six Nations
Rugby.summary: Ireland's 2027 Women's Six Nations encounter with England will be played at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin.
Rugby.body:
Ireland's 2027 Women's Six Nations encounter with England will be played at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin. Scott Bemand's side made their Six Nations debut at the Aviva Stadium with a win over Scotland in this year's competition and will welcome the world champions to Dublin in the fourth round of fixtures on 8 May.

A crowd of 31,294 watched the 54-5 win over Scotland in May, a record crowd for a women's match in Ireland. "Playing at Aviva Stadium last season was an incredible and landmark experience for the group and we're really excited to be returning to the home of Irish rugby in 2027," said Ireland captain Erin King.

Earlier this year, Scott Bemand’s team played their first-ever standalone fixture at the venue against Scotland and welcomed a record crowd of 31,294 to the venue. At the same Championship, the world champion Red Roses hosted Ireland at Allianz Stadium and saw a crowd of 77,120 make its way to West London.

It has also been confirmed that Ireland’s Round 2 fixture against France will be hosted at Galway’s Dexcom Stadium. Last weekend, Ireland beat Japan 31-24 at the venue and got their first win of WXV Global Series 2026.

Rugby.title: Tickets go on sale for historic first British & Irish Lions Women tour
Rugby.summary: Tickets for Test fixtures at next year's first-ever British & Irish Lions Women tour in New Zealand have gone on sale.
Rugby.body:
Tickets for the inaugural British & Irish Lions Women’s Tour of New Zealand have gone on sale. In September 2027 the inaugural British & Irish Lions Women squad, comprised of the best players from England, Ireland, Scotland and Wales will take on the Black Ferns in three Tests in New Zealand.

For a limited time, Test matches taking place in Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch will have selected children’s tickets priced at NZD$1 and adult tickets cost NZD$27. The first Test will take place at Auckland’s Mount Smart Stadium, then Wellington Memorial Stadium a week later and the series will conclude at Te Kaha in Christchurch. Tour fixtures against the Black Ferns XV and the Invitational XV will take place in Whangarei and Hamilton.

Rugby.summary: Exeter boss Rob Baxter says prop Josh Iosefa-Scott is likely to move to France when his contract ends next summer.
Rugby.body:
Exeter Chiefs director of rugby Rob Baxter says prop Josh Iosefa-Scott is likely move to France when his contract ends next summer. Reports in France have linked the 30-year-old tight-head with a move to Provence after six seasons at Sandy Park.

The English-qualified New Zealander has played 99 games in all competitions for the Chiefs since moving from Waikato in the summer of 2021. "I haven't had any confirmation of whatever club he's going to," Baxter told BBC Sport of the prop, whose current deal runs out in the summer.

Rugby.summary: Peter O’Mahony has picked Andy Farrell over Rassie Erasmus as the best coach he worked under, despite offering a glowing assessment of the Springbok boss’ coaching ability.
Rugby.body:
Peter O’Mahony has picked Andy Farrell over Rassie Erasmus as the best coach he worked under, despite offering a glowing assessment of the Springbok boss’ coaching ability. The former Ireland and Munster captain was speaking on the For the Love of Rugby podcast following the release of his book All In, having worked closely with both Farrell and Erasmus during his career.

While Erasmus initially arrived at Munster in more of an overarching director of rugby role, O’Mahony explained that the South African was also an accomplished hands-on coach when circumstances required him to take a greater role on the training field following the death of Anthony Foley.

Rugby.title: 'The Wallabies moved several steps closer to cracking the Springboks' DNA code'
Rugby.summary: Australia picked up where New Zealand left off in unearthing more of the tools which could stop South Africa's charge for a third straight Rugby World Cup.
Rugby.body:
The fictional scientists in the 1993 blockbuster Jurrasic Park use frog DNA to gap-fill broken dinosaur code extracted from prehistoric mosquitoes and fabricate their very own version of the real thing. If there is a complete DNA strand of ‘how to beat the world champions at rugby’ waiting to be discovered somewhere deep underground, frozen in amber, nobody has yet unearthed it. The All Blacks found some parts in the recent Greatest Rivalry series, the Wallabies dug up rather more at the weekend. But nobody yet has the complete code, despite Australia’s nail-biting 42-38 victory at the Optus Stadium in Perth.

There is no doubt the science is moving closer to finding an answer, and the pack are gaining ground on the Springboks. The idea there are two or even three potential South African teams waiting in the wings to bring home ‘Bill’ for a World Cup-winning three-peat next year was thoroughly exposed as the fiction it truly is.

Rugby.title: England's Underhill to miss autumn internationals
Rugby.summary: England and Bath flanker Sam Underhill is out for months with a ruptured biceps that requires surgery.
Rugby.body:
England flanker Sam Underhill will miss the Nations Championship this autumn after rupturing his biceps in Bath's opening Prem game away at Harlequins. Underhill went off in the 48th minute of the win at The Stoop and was seen at the end of the game with strapping around his arm, which will require surgery later this week.

Bath expect the 30-year-old to be out until December or January, meaning he will miss a large portion of the domestic season as well as England's three internationals against Australia, Japan and New Zealand in November.

Rugby.summary: Cardiff fly-half Callum Sheedy says he did not realise his "header" against Scarlets in the United Rugby Championship (URC) game would go viral.
Rugby.body:
Cardiff fly-half Callum Sheedy says he did not realise his "header" against Scarlets in the United Rugby Championship (URC) game would go viral. Sheedy headed the ball forward after chasing his own kick in the second half of the 21-15 victory against Scarlets on Saturday night.

The clip has had more than 800,000 hits across social media. "I probably wasn't thinking at the time, that was the problem," said Sheedy. "I remember the ball sitting up, and I could see Blair [Murray] coming towards me, and I thought it was going be an aerial contest.

Rugby.title: Ex-Kelso and Gala fly-half Craig Dods named as head coach of Canada’s rugby sevens team
Rugby.summary: Ex-Kelso and Gala fly-half Craig Dods named as head coach of Canada’s rugby sevens team The Southern Reporter
Rugby.body:
Ex-Kelso and Gala fly-half Craig Dods has been appointed as head coach of Canada’s rugby sevens squad and as an assistant to their national XVs team. The 34-year-old, also a former development officer at the Poynder Park and Netherdale clubs, joins Rugby Canada after four years working for the Scottish Rugby Union as a specialist kicking coach.

“I’m delighted to be joining Rugby Canada at a pivotal time for the sport in such a proud and passionate rugby country,” said the Borderer, son of 23-times-capped Scotland full-back Peter Dods.

Rugby.summary: Craig Dods has left Scottish Rugby to join Rugby Canada's coaching setup as head coach of Canada's men's sevens team and assistant coach of the men's 15s team.
Rugby.body:
Craig Dods has left Scottish Rugby to join Rugby Canada’s coaching setup as head coach of Canada’s men’s sevens team and assistant coach of the men’s 15s team. The son of Peter Dods, a mainstay of the great Scotland 1984 Grand Slam-winning team and a British and Irish Lions tourist, was chosen from a long list of 70 applicants.

He comes into the role after serving as Scottish Rugby’s specialist skills coach, GB7s assistant coach and as a national talent pathway coach for Scottish Rugby. Previously, he has worked for Gala and Kelso in the Scottish Borders, as well as heading up Hungary’s women’s rugby programme for a couple of years,leading them to their best-ever finish on the Rugby Europe Sevens circuit.

The South African also did not speak to the media before, during or after the opening-weekend victory at Leicester. The Daily Telegraph reported earlier on Tuesday, external that Venter "resigned" as director of rugby last month and took up a new role of "head of rugby culture and wine consultant", with head coach Joe Shaw assuming responsibility for media commitments.

Rugby.summary: Springbok Women prop Xoliswa Khuzwayo has admitted that her team don't mind being called the "underdogs".
Rugby.body:
Springbok Women prop Xoliswa Khuzwayo has admitted that her team don’t mind being called the “underdogs”. It has now been a year since South Africa stunned the world with their run to the Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 quarter-finals and established themselves as a team to watch across the current World Cup cycle.

At the start of the year South Africa admitted that their aim is not to move further up the World Rugby rankings. Currently ranked 10th, the side have been challenged at WXV Global Series and started their autumn campaign with a loss to Wales in Cardiff, before they got back to winning ways with a 41-27 win against Italy in Pordenone.

Rugby.title: Johann van Graan's worst fears confirmed over Sam Underhill injury
Rugby.summary: The England flanker will have an operation on Thursday to repair the bicep he tore in last Friday's 33-17 win at Harlequins.
Rugby.body:
Johann van Graan has revealed that England flanker Sam Underhill suffered a torn bicep in last Friday’s 33-17 win at Harlequins and will undergo an operation on Thursday. Underhill was replaced after 48 minutes at the Twickenham Stoop and a concerned van Graan rushed down to the tunnel to check on the luckless player, later admitting that the injury looked “potentially serious.”

Now his worst fears have been confirmed, with Underhill’s latest setback likely to cost him three months of rugby, including England’s Nations Championship campaign in November.

Rugby.title: Sale camp deliver early bad news for England after PREM opening round

Rugby.body:
England boss Steve Borthwick has been dealt a Nations Championship blow after Sale Sharks loosehead Bevan Rodd underwent a fourth operation in two years following a hand injury sustained against Bristol Bears last weekend.

Rodd, who made five appearances off the bench in last season’s Six Nations, faces eight to 12 weeks on the sidelines after an operation on the scaphoid, the most commonly fractured carpal bone in the hand.

Rugby.summary: Premiership Women's Rugby champions Saracens have announced the retention of Wales internationals Georgia Evans and Donna Rose.
Rugby.body:
JAECOO Premiership Women’s Rugby champions Saracens have announced the retention of Wales internationals Georgia Evans and Donna Rose. Evans joined the club in 2020 and has been a key performer for the team in recent years. Capable of playing in the second row or back row, the 29-year-old made her 50th Test appearance for Wales last weekend against the USA Women’s Eagles in Cardiff.

Last season, she made 17 PWR appearances for the North London club as they won the English league title for the first time since 2022. Alex Austerberry, Director of Rugby, said: “Georgia is approaching 100 games for the club. This is testament to her quality as a player. Those appearances have come across the back five, which illustrates her versatility and ability to play in such abrasive and competitive positions at the highest level.

Rugby.title: Saracens bend the rules with bizarre Brendan Venter job title change
Rugby.summary: Saracens have responded to being fined for Brendan Venter's refusal to carry out media duties by changing his job title to “head of rugby culture and wine consultant”.
Rugby.body:
Saracens have responded to being fined for Brendan Venter’s refusal to carry out media duties by changing his job title to “head of rugby culture and wine consultant”. As Director of Rugby, the job title still given to him on Saracens’ official website, the South African is honour bound by PREM Rugby regulations to speak to the press.

However, Saracens say they asked the league’s organisers permission in July for head coach Shaw to be their designated media person. Shaw took Venter’s place at the pre-season content capture day at Allianz Stadium earler this month and has continued to fulfil those obligations, speaking to TNT Sports during their coverage of the London club’s impressive 40-38 victory at Mattioli Woods Welford Road on Sunday.

Rugby.title: ‘No-one could remember such a crazy game. Or explain that last 10 minutes. No matter.'
Rugby.summary: Five tries each, four yellow cards in the final 10 minutes and frayed nerves aplenty - relive the drama of Australia's win over South Africa.
Rugby.body:
The Wallabies have recorded the craziest win in living memory… feels like the sort of thing to say after that absolutely bonkers 42-38 win over South Africa in Perth on Sunday.

But then I had to check to see if I said the same thing after the Wallabies’ memorable 38-22 win at Ellis Park last August. I hadn’t, as it turned out, but Sunday still might only have been the craziest win in… well, a year.

Rugby.title: Jack Willis addresses Test future as eligibility for England rival nears
Rugby.summary: Jack Willis has admitted an England return remains “something I still want to do” after being named Top 14 Player of the Year for the second season in a row.
Rugby.body:
Jack Willis has admitted an England return remains “something I still want to do” after being named Top 14 Player of the Year for the second season in a row. The Toulouse flanker, who starred in the Top 14 final victory over Montpellier in June, joined club-mate Antoine Dupont as the only player to win the honour twice, having beaten Bordeaux-Begles and France fly-half Matthieu Jalibert and ASM Clermont-Auvergne’s All Black Harry Plummer to this year’s prize.

Willis’ success in France has come at the cost of his England career, with the 29-year-old remaining ineligible for selection under the RFU’s overseas policy after choosing to stay at Toulouse.

Rugby.title: Red Roses to return to Sunderland for Women's Six Nations
Rugby.summary: England will return to Sunderland's Stadium of Light – the venue for their record-breaking Women's Rugby World Cup opener – for the 2027 Six Nations.
Rugby.body:
England will return to Sunderland's Stadium of Light - the venue for their record-breaking Women's Rugby World Cup opener - in their first home match of the 2027 Six Nations. The Red Roses will play Scotland at the venue on 17 April.

It will be the first time they have played a home match away from a rugby-specific ground outside of a World Cup. England drew 42,723 fans to the Stadium of Light for the 67-9 victory over the United States that opened the Women's Rugby World Cup in August 2025.

Rugby.summary: The former Northampton fly-half enjoyed a dream debut for his new club on the weekend, helping them open their BKT URC campaign with a 34-29 bonus point victory away to Ulster Rugby.
Rugby.body:
After a whirlwind of a summer, James Grayson has made a storming start with Edinburgh Rugby. The former Northampton fly-half enjoyed a dream debut for his new club on the weekend, helping them open their BKT URC campaign with a 34-29 bonus point victory away to Ulster Rugby.

He brought assured tactical control at No 10 and also landed six shots at goal during Friday’s night’s notable triumph in Belfast. The son of former England international Paul Grayson, the 28-year-old has come on board from Japanese club Mitsubishi Dynaboars, having previously had a long spell with the Saints.

Rugby.title: Bath's Boxing Day game with Leicester moved back a day
Rugby.summary: Bath's Boxing Day Prem Rugby fixture with Leicester Tigers is moved to 27 December.
Rugby.body:
Bath's Boxing Day Prem Rugby fixture with Leicester Tigers has been moved to Sunday, 27 December. The game - in round eight of the Prem - had been due to take place at 15:05 GMT at the Recreation Ground.

But it has been moved to 17:30 GMT a day later because of travel restrictions across the city - there are no rail or Park and Ride services running on Boxing Day in Bath. There will still be two games on Boxing Day, which falls on a Saturday this year, as Bristol host Newcastle Red Bulls at 15:00 GMT and Gloucester travel to Sale at 17:30 GMT.

The former Bok captain felt the Wallabies got the better of South Africa in an area they have traditionally dominated, something he admitted was unusual for a side that has built so much of its success around kicking pressure and contests in the air.

Rugby.summary: Former England captain Lawrence Dallaglio is set to sell his 2003 Rugby World Cup winner's medal after being declared bankrupt.
Rugby.body:
Former England captain Lawrence Dallaglio is set to sell his 2003 Rugby World Cup winner's medal after being declared bankrupt. The 54-year-old has put a number of items from his illustrious career up for auction including medals, trophies and caps.

The World Cup medal is expected to raise between £50,000 and £80,000 while in total the collection has an estimated value of £180,000. Dallaglio was one of the stars of the England side that won the World Cup in dramatic fashion against Australia 23 years ago.

Rugby.title: ‘Problem solve on the run’: Inside the Wallabies’ 11-man fight for victory
Rugby.summary: Jeremy Williams took over the captaincy as an undermanned Wallabies looked to protect their lead against the Springboks in Perth.
Rugby.body:
Jeremy Williams took over the captaincy as an undermanned Wallabies looked to protect their lead against the Springboks in Perth. It was a 25-point ball game with less than 15 minutes left, but four yellow cards and three converted tries had the Test in the balance.

“Problem solve on the run,” Williams explained post-game, after the Wallabies hung on for a 42-38 win, despite going down to 11 men. Harry Wilson, Ryan Lonergan, Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii and Hunter Paisami had been shown yellow cards during the final quarter.

Rugby.body:
All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie has revealed the conversations he had with former captain Scott Barrett before naming Ardie Savea as the team’s captain, after Barrett was named in the upcoming Bledisloe Cup squad.

Rennie’s 34-man squad to take on the Wallabies featured several notable inclusions, with Shannon Frizell and Barrett returning to the All Blacks for the first time in 2026. Barrett’s inclusion to the 34-man squad squeezed out Blues lock Sam Darry, while Patrick Tuipulotu is also missing, but through injury.

Rugby.title: The best matches from the inaugural Ultimate Sevens season
Rugby.summary: RugbyPass looks back on six matches that stood out across the three legs of the Ultimate Sevens.
Rugby.body:
The inaugural season of the Ultimate Sevens has ended, and with it, a chance to examine and assess its impact on sevens rugby at large. The new format and teams allowed for a new style of sevens to be played, one that showcased the talents of many of the world’s best coming together.

With that in mind, RugbyPass looks back on six matches that stood out across the three legs of the Ultimate Sevens, and who stood up in the key moments to deliver results. Despite going down in the final to Clan Taran, Foudre Bleue signalled themselves early on in the three series, with this match marking the first golden try scored in the tournament’s history.

Rugby.title: Zimbabwe land SVNS 3 qualification with Rugby Africa 7s title
Rugby.summary: The Zimbabwe men’s sevens team has fired a warning shot to the rest of Africa’s rapidly developing sevens nations by stunning hosts Uganda.
Rugby.body:
The Zimbabwe men’s sevens team has fired a warning shot to the rest of Africa’s rapidly developing sevens nations, stunning hosts Uganda 26-19 to claim the Rugby Africa 7s title at Kyadondo Rugby Grounds in Kampala.

The result will see the Cheetahs earn qualification for the HSBC SVNS 3 tournament later this year, but it was far from guaranteed after a tightly contested weekend. Starting their tournament with a 19-12 win against Morocco, Zimbabwe got into their groove with a 40-17 win over Ghana.

Rugby.body:
Free-scoring All Blacks wing Fehi Fineanganofo has convinced Newcastle Red Bulls to delay his arrival on Tyneside so he can chase his dream of playing at the Rugby World Cup. It was originally announced back in January that the 24-year-old had agreed a two-year deal with Newcastle, beginning at the start of the current campaign.

Rugby.body:
The Wallaroos have jumped up two places in the World Rugby rankings thanks to their 30-10 victory over Scotland in Edinburgh. Led by Director of Women’s High Performance Tim Walsh during the WXV Global Series, alongside a number of interim coaches ahead of Sione Fukofuka’s arrival as head coach in January, the side played their second Test of the year against the Scots at Hive Stadium.

It was an historic afternoon for the women in gold. Michaela Leonard became the first player to earn 50 caps for the Wallaroos, while Desiree Miller’s try saw her become the first player to gain 100 Test points for the team.

Rugby.title: Noah Brown: Brive's 6ft 9ins, 124kg teen eligible for England and the Springboks and targeting Test rugby
Rugby.summary: Six months ago, the giant 19-year-old had no club and scant prospects. Now he's signed up in France and picquing the interest of Rassie Erasmus.
Rugby.body:
In just a few wild months, Noah Brown’s dreams have begun to come true. He has gone from club-less and stymied in England, to attracting suitors at the very top of French rugby, piquing the interest of the game’s thought leader, Rassie Erasmus, and training with Courtney Lawes, the ageless England hitman. As he sat on Zoom calls this spring with some of the biggest teams in Europe, the 19-year-old found it hard to process how drastically, and how swiftly, his life was changing.

Brown is a second-row with an eye-catching profile and ambition to match his size. He stands 6ft 9ins tall and weighs 124kg. Even in the age of protein-infused He-Men, those are mighty numbers. He was born in Port Elizabeth to a South African mother and English father, raised in Greater London, and holds eligibility for both nations. Brown is hungry to wear the colours of either U20s team, a point he hammers home repeatedly. Fresh from Oxford College, he has signed for Brive in the ProD2 and begun his first season with the club’s espoirs (effectively, academy) side.

Rugby.summary: Old names, new looks and some stunning scores marked the return of the Prem for another season.
Rugby.body:

Sarries were short of domination - the lead swapped hands four times in the final half hour of a blockbuster - but victory away at Leicester was a fine statement of intent. Hobbled by an injury to Olly Hartley in the first half and then reduced to 14 men by Nick Isiekwe's 20-minute red card in the second, the visitors nonetheless dug deep and silenced the baying Tigers fans with an extraordinary 40-38 win.

Rugby.title: Boks escape creating two unwanted records in Perth defeat
Rugby.summary: To score five tries and 38 points and still lose a Test match is rare, especially for a team of the calibre of world champions South Africa.
Rugby.body:
The 1999 Rugby World Cup-winning Wallabies famously lifted the Webb Ellis Cup in Cardiff having only conceded a now unthinkable one try all tournament, with the United States surprisingly the team to deny them a complete shut-out.

Back then the mantra of defence wins championships rung true, but not any more. “I remember coaching a team in Wales who went five games without conceding one try, and that’s impossible now. It is for the better of the game,” acknowledged defence coach guru Shaun Edwards earlier this year.

Rugby.title: The major caveat hanging over the Springboks' defeat in Perth
Rugby.summary: Australia deserved every second of its celebration in Perth. The Wallabies scored five tries against the world champions, led 42-17 with a quarter of an hour left...
Rugby.body:
Australia deserved every second of its celebration in Perth. The Wallabies scored five tries against the world champions, led 42-17 with a quarter of an hour left, and somehow survived the closing minutes with four players in the sin bin. Len Ikitau was outstanding, Joseph-Aukuso Sua’ali’i helped win the aerial contest, and Les Kiss’s side looked quicker and more forceful for most of the match. The 42-38 final score flatters South Africa and there can be no question that the deserving team took the spoils.

It may prove an important night for Australian rugby. A home World Cup is approaching, and this was a victory around which players and supporters can build belief. The Guardian described it as the match Australian rugby needed. One could make the case that it is the best result in Australian rugby for over a decade. But that is looking at this story from David’s perspective. For Goliath, it is but a flesh wound.

Rugby.body:
Exeter Chiefs director of rugby Rob Baxter hopes he will see a reaction from his side after their surprising 45-24 home loss to Gloucester. Last season's beaten Prem finalists began the new season by conceding seven tries as a bout of illness went through the home camp.

It was a biggest home loss in any competition since Bordeaux hammered a struggling Exeter side 69-17 at Sandy Park in a Champions Cup fixture in January 2025 . "You've got to be really careful that you don't assume things are going quite well and actually you've got to put your foot down because it's a game of Premiership rugby and you have to work extremely hard to make good things happen," Baxter told BBC Radio Devon.

The incident is recounted in O’Mahony’s new autobiography, All In, as he reflects on one of the bleakest days of his international career. Ireland were thrashed 60-0 in Hamilton in the third Test of a winless summer tour, a result that remains one of the heaviest defeats in the history of Irish rugby.

Rugby.title: Rassie Erasmus explains emptying the Bok bench on 47 minutes in Perth
Rugby.summary: Rassie Erasmus insisted South Africa's unprecedented decision to unload their entire bench in the 47th minute against Australia was a reaction...
Rugby.body:
Rassie Erasmus insisted South Africa’s unprecedented decision to unload their entire bench in the 47th minute against Australia was a reaction to events rather than a move that had been mapped out before kick-off.

The Wallabies led 24-17 at the break and stretched that advantage to 42-17 after 65 minutes. While the Springboks mounted a late fightback and closed to within four points, Erasmus said the decision to deploy all eight replacements at once was driven by the flow of the match.

Rugby.title: Gloucester wanted to lay down marker
Rugby.summary: New Gloucester captain Dewi Lake says the side wanted to lay down a marker in their opening Prem game at Exeter.
Rugby.body:
New Gloucester captain Dewi Lake said the side wanted to lay down a marker in their opening Prem game as they produced a dominant and shock victory away at Exeter. The Cherry and Whites were confident winners against the Chiefs, beating the 2025-26 Prem finalists 45-24 on their own pitch for a first win at Sandy Park in 12 years.

Lake, who arrived at the club this summer from Ospreys, scored two tries and was named man of the match. "We spoke about laying a marker down, we spoke about mindset a lot of the week, we spoke about what we wanted to do and i think we delivered that," Lake told BBC Radio Gloucestershire.

Rugby.title: Fifteen vs Eleven! It's happened before in Test rugby
Rugby.summary: Australia's 42-38 win over the world champions Springboks was remarkable in many ways, not least for the four yellow cards received by the Wallabies
Rugby.body:
It was a game seemingly like no other, one watched in disbelief by the 54,678 present at the Optus Stadium in Perth and the millions watching on devices at home. Australia’s 42-38 win over the world champions Springboks was remarkable in many ways, not least for the four yellow cards received by the Wallabies in a chaotic seven-minute spell between the 68th and 75th minutes.

As our man on the spot, Finn Morton, reported, the Wallabies went down to 13 after yellow cards in quick succession to Harry Wilson and Ryan Lonergan, before Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii and then Hunter Paisami joined them in the over-crowded sin bin.

Rugby.title: URC table: Irish sides hit 16 year low as South Africans and Scots sitting pretty
Rugby.summary: The opening round of the new BKT URC season saw a clean-sweep for South Africa and Scotland, while it was a rare winless weekend for Ireland.
Rugby.body:
The opening round of the new BKT URC season saw a clean-sweep for South Africa and Scotland, while it was a rare winless weekend for Ireland. It’s actually the first time since 2009 that all four Irish sides have lost on the first weekend of the league campaign.

In a further rarity, there were just two home wins from the eight matches, bucking the traditional trend in the competition. One of those solitary successes on home soil was recorded by the 10Bet Lions who claimed a notable scalp by beating reigning champions Leinster Rugby 27-26 in Johannesburg.

Rugby.summary: Double World Cup-winning Springbok Steven Kitshoff has asserted that South Africa could have 15 injuries at next year's World Cup and still win an unprecedented third title in a row.
Rugby.body:
Double World Cup-winning Springbok Steven Kitshoff has asserted that South Africa could have 15 injuries at next year’s World Cup and still win an unprecedented third title in a row.

A Springboks squad that had seen 13 changes from the XV that started the final Test against the All Blacks in Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry narrowly lost to Australia 42-38 on Sunday, almost overturning a 42-17 second-half deficit in the final 15 minutes in Perth to come within a whisker of snatching victory with the final play of the match.

'He’s physical for a guy that doesn’t look physical... he can basically do any sport well' Jamie Dobie has hailed Glasgow’s comeback win away to Munster as an “awesome start to the season” after marking his century with a try double.

Rugby.title: Chaotic ending robs Wallabies of world rankings 4-year high
Rugby.summary: When Australia led South Africa 42-17 with 17 minutes left to go, it looked for all the world that they would beat the Springboks by a big enough margin to leapfrog both Scotland and England.
Rugby.body:
When Australia led South Africa 42-17 with 17 minutes left to go, it looked for all the world that they would beat the Springboks by a big enough margin to leapfrog both Scotland and England and move up to fifth in the World Rugby Men’s Rankings.

However, the concession of four yellow cards – the most the Wallabies have ever received in a single Test – put paid to that notion, and instead they were glad to hang on to a precious 42-38 victory against the world champions.

Rugby.title: Pirates concede record 73-point haul at Coventry
Rugby.summary: Cornish Pirates joint-head coach Gavin Cattle says his side are not as bad as their 73-40 defeat at Coventry would suggest.
Rugby.body:
Cornish Pirates joint-head coach Gavin Cattle says his side are not as bad as their 73-40 defeat at Coventry would suggest. Pirates conceded 11 tries as they let in a club-record amount of points in a Champ fixture, four more than in their record 69-8 loss to Worcester Warriors in April 2015.

Pirates were hampered by centre Joe Elderkin being injured in the warm-up. They had fly-half Arwel Robson and replacement forward Matt Cannon yellow carded within three minutes of one another early in the second half as they conceded five tries in a 13-minute period surrounding the duo entering the sin bin.

Rugby.title: The Wallabies’ three biggest concerns ahead of All Blacks clash at Eden Park
Rugby.summary: Hunter Paisami and Len Ikitau, the trusted centre combination which first took shape under Dave Rennie, has now returned, and boy do they look better many caps later.
Rugby.body:
The Wallabies have done the unthinkable by putting 42 points on the Springboks in Perth; it is a statement scoreline by the now sixth-ranked Wallabies. For all the talk about officiating, downed communications, and substitution confusion, the Wallabies nevertheless found a way to score five tries and three penalty goals, all adding up to 42 points.

The Wallabies had the Springboks dead to rights with just 10 minutes left in the game, 42 points to 17, a margin of 25 points, or more than three converted tries. Anyway you cut it, the Wallabies were dominant over this heavily reshuffled Springboks side.

Rugby.summary: The talking points as Dragons draw, Ospreys lose and Cardiff take the derby bragging rights against Scarlets on the opening weekend of the URC.
Rugby.body:
The Welsh men's rugby season is back, with mixed results for the four professional sides. Cardiff triumphed against Scarlets in the opening United Rugby Championship (URC) Welsh derby, draw specialists Dragons again shared the spoils, while Ospreys came unstuck in South Africa but did claim a four-try bonus.

Welsh exports in England made the headlines in the Prem, with Gloucester new boys Dewi Lake and Jac Morgan demonstrating what Ospreys were missing. BBC Sport looks back at the opening URC weekend and casts an eye on the Welsh players starring in England's top flight.

Rugby.summary: Saracens head coach Joe Shaw believes his team’s dramatic victory at Leicester Tigers was down to them staying cool despite the adversity they faced.
Rugby.body:
Saracens head coach Joe Shaw believes his team’s dramatic victory at Leicester Tigers was down to them staying cool despite the adversity they faced. In their opening Gallagher PREM fixture of the season, Sarries lost centre Olly Hartley to an arm injury early in proceedings and flanker Nick Isiekwe to a 20-minute red card in the second half.

They also had to fight from behind twice against a fired-up Leicester – for whom Gabriel Hamer-Webb scored a hat-trick – with Rotimi Segun’s 73rd-minute try deciding a breathless contest at Mattioli Woods Welford Road.

Rugby.title: 'We take full accountability': Kévin Rouet laments Canada performance in La Rochelle
Rugby.summary: Canada head coach Kévin Rouet cut a frustrated figure at full-time of his team's 21-5 loss to France in La Rochelle.
Rugby.body:
Canada head coach Kévin Rouet cut a frustrated figure at full-time of his team’s 21-5 loss to France in La Rochelle. The 39-year-old watched his team struggle to make an impact against François Ratier’s team on the French west coast, as the hosts controlled the fixture from start to finish. Simply put, Canada were outclassed.

An Émilie Boulard brace, a try from Alexandra Chambon and conversions from Carla Arbez and Lina Queyroi cancelled out Lizzie Gibson’s 35th-minute try. While Gibson has seen her stock rise with four tries in three WXV Global Series fixtures this autumn, the overall performance was a stark contrast to the 26-all draw with England a week prior and their 10-try win against Scotland a fortnight prior.

Rugby.title: South Africa suffer double injury blow ahead of Spain fixture
Rugby.summary: South Africa will be without all-time leading points scorer Libbie Janse van Rensburg for their WXV Global Series crossover fixture in Seville next weekend.
Rugby.body:
South Africa will be without all-time leading points scorer Libbie Janse van Rensburg for their WXV Global Series crossover fixture in Seville next weekend. The Springbok Women playmaker has returned home with an ankle injury sustained in her team’s 41-29 victory over Italy on Saturday.

To replace Janse van Rensburg, co-head coaches Laurian Johannes-Haupt and Franzel September have called Mary Zulu into camp. Zulu, 23, has not won a Test cap since the Rugby Africa Women’s Cup triumph earlier this year. She did, however, captain a South Africa A team on a two-match tour of Brazil last month. In 18 Test appearances, Zulu has scored 45 points.

Rugby.summary: Saracens overcome a second-half red card for Nick Isiekwe to begin the Brendan Venter era with a 40-38 win at Leicester Tigers.
Rugby.body:
Saracens overcame a second-half red card for Nick Isiekwe to begin the Brendan Venter era with a seesaw 40-38 win at Leicester Tigers. Two tries from wing Rotimi Segun with Sarries short-handed saw the visitors prevail in a breathless 12-try affair at Welford Road.

Gabriel Hamer-Webb scored a hat-trick for Leicester, but it was to no avail as Venter's second stint in charge at Saracens got away to the perfect start. Venter's colourful first spell in charge brought a series of disciplinary run-ins, but set the foundations for the success that followed under Mark McCall.

Rugby.summary: The Wallaroos were delighted to finish off their “tough” European tour with a win over Scotland in the WXV Global Series.
Rugby.body:
The Wallaroos were delighted to finish off their “tough” European tour with a win over Scotland in the WXV Global Series. Over the past fortnight, Australia have lost out to England and France, but ended their time in the northern hemisphere with a 30-10 victory against Dave Butchers’ Scotland in Edinburgh.

Desiree Miller, Samantha Wood, Brianna Hoy and Faitala Moleka were all try-scorers in the Scottish capital as the visitors overturned a 10-5 half-time deficit to subject their hosts to a third loss in a row this September.

Rugby.summary: Ireland held on to a 31-24 victory over Japan in the WXV Global Series at Dexcom Stadium in Galway.
Rugby.body:
Ireland held on to a 31-24 victory over Japan in the WXV Global Series at Dexcom Stadium in Galway. Two tries each from player of the match Brittany Hogan and Ireland’s new all-time women’s try scorer Béibhinn Parsons, as well as a score from Aoife Dalton, saw Scott Bemand’s side bounce back from their 40-36 defeat by the USA Women’s Eagles last week.

The Sakura Fifteen fought hard and dotted down for four tries, with Moe Nagaoka crashing over twice, Nijiho Nagata registered her team’s third from a maul and 18-year-old Nami Asari got over the whitewash in the closing stages.

Rugby.title: Talking points: 'Patchy' Ireland found a way to beat Japan in Galway
Rugby.summary: Ireland returned to winning ways in the WXV Global Series, rebounding from last week’s defeat to the USA Women's Eagles in Dublin with a 31-24 victory over Japan in Galway.
Rugby.body:
Ireland returned to winning ways in the WXV Global Series, rebounding from last week’s defeat to the USA Women’s Eagles in Dublin with a 31-24 victory over Japan in Galway. With the wind a prominent factor throughout, Ireland played with the breeze in the first half and opened up 19-5 half-time lead.

Perhaps unsurprisingly, Japan worked back into the contest after the break, scoring three second half tries when playing with the elements. However, Aoife Dalton and Ireland’s new record try-scorer Béibhinn Parsons crossed at crucial times, capitalising on Sakura Fifteen errors to ensure the hosts had enough to withstand the comeback.

Rugby.summary: Wales may have suffered another Test defeat, but Sean Lynn's new-look side has given fans plenty to be optimistic about before next month's trip to Japan.
Rugby.body:
It was another defeat for Wales, but this one feels different. As many of the three thousand-plus fans exited Cardiff Arms Park after the USA claimed a 26-24 victory, I assume they did so with a sense of optimism rather than the doom and gloom that often surrounds Welsh rugby.

What head coach Sean Lynn and his backroom staff have done to this group in just six weeks of pre-season is to be applauded. Wales have been transformed from a side which whimpered out of a winless World Cup and Six Nations into a competitive 80-minute team and one the nation can truly get behind.

Rugby.title: Rassie Erasmus had a few words for the officials amid Perth chaos
Rugby.summary: Rassie Erasmus refused to reach for excuses or a gruelling Rugby Championship schedule after South Africa's dramatic 42-38 defeat to Australia in Perth.
Rugby.body:
Rassie Erasmus refused to reach for excuses or a gruelling Rugby Championship schedule after South Africa’s dramatic 42-38 defeat to Australia in Perth. Despite the match being repeatedly disrupted by reviews, communication problems and a remarkable period where the Wallabies were reduced to just 11 men by referee Andrea Piardi, the Springbok boss insisted the result came down to his side’s own shortcomings.

Erasmus admitted South Africa had “rolled the dice” with an experimental selection and accepted Australia were the better team on the night, while also going out of his way to praise Piardi and his team of officials for managing a chaotic contest under difficult circumstances.

Rugby.title: Four men down
Rugby.summary: Australia are reduced to 11 men but dig in for a remarkable win against a much-changed South Africa side as they beat the world champions 42-38 in Perth.
Rugby.body:
Australia were reduced to 11 men but dug in for an extraordinary win against a much-changed South Africa side as they beat the world champions 42-38 in Perth. The Wallabies excelled with some vibrant attacking rugby, scoring five tries against the back-to-back World Cup winners to lead by 25 points with 16 minutes left.

But then a manic spell of four yellow cards in nine minutes left the hosts overrun, with South Africa mounting a comeback that ultimately fell just short. The visitors made 13 changes after beating New Zealand in Baltimore but still fielded a strong starting XV, which boasted 240 caps in the second row alone.

Rugby.title: Len Ikitau stars as 11-man Wallabies survive incredible Springboks fightback
Rugby.summary: Harry Potter and Fraser McReight's carries close to the line set up their fourth try, through the skipper, Harry Wilson.
Rugby.body:
Les Kiss’ Wallabies have held on to beat the Springboks, 42-38, at Perth’s Optus Stadium on Sunday in an utterly captivating Test match. The Wallabies, who at one stage in the final ten minutes were down to eleven players, kept Rassie Erasmus’ Springboks out at the death to clinch an incredible victory over the back-to-back World Champions.

With the victory, the Wallabies clinched the Mandela Challenge Plate, continuing their unbeaten streak under Kiss in 2026. The 2025 John Eales medalist, Len Ikitau, was among the Wallabies’ best before succumbing to an ankle injury in the 53rd minute, crossing for a double in the first 40 minutes.

Rugby.title: Women's rugby continues to grow one year on from Women's Rugby World Cup 2025
Rugby.summary: Today marks one year to the day since England's Red Roses beat Canada in the Women's Rugby World Cup 2025 final.
Rugby.body:
Today marks one year to the day since England’s Red Roses beat Canada in the Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 final. In front of a world record crowd of 81,885 at Allianz Stadium, John Mitchell’s side ended their 11-year wait to be world champions again with tries from Ellie Kildunne, Amy Cokayne, Abbie Ward and an Alex Matthews brace.

Now, the world of women’s Test rugby is engulfed by WXV Global Series – which has provided scintillating action for the past weekends – an annual event that will see the world’s top 18 teams play more than 100 international fixtures between 2026 and 2028.

Rugby.summary: Bristol director of rugby Pat Lam was beaming with pride after his side opened their Prem campaign with an impressive 34-24 bonus-point victory at Sale.
Rugby.body:
Bristol director of rugby Pat Lam was beaming with pride after his side opened their Prem campaign with an impressive 34-24 bonus-point victory at Sale. The hosts touched down through hooker Luke Cowan-Dickie and a brace from winger Tom O’Flaherty but Bears duo Louis Rees-Zammit and Harry Randall both scored twice before team-mate Tomas Gwilliam added a late fifth.

The result saw Bristol lay down an impressive marker in Salford and left Lam delighted. The Bears boss said: “We know that it’s such a hard place to come and win up here, so I’m very pleased and proud of the boys.

Rugby.title: Shedding and raising pounds
Rugby.summary: Former Wales prop Adam Jones will face one of his greatest challenges when he tackles the Cardiff half-marathon.
Rugby.body:
Former Wales prop Adam Jones achieved a lot in his glittering career as he became one of Welsh rugby's most recognisable cult heroes. He is a three-time Grand Slam champion and a British and Irish Lions series winner, making 100 international appearances before retiring in 2018.

Jones will concede he was known for his scrummaging prowess rather than his running exploits. Now aged 45, Jones will tackle one of the most significant physical tests of his life when he takes on the Cardiff half-marathon on Sunday, 4 October.

Rugby.title: A day for the ages, a moment for the girls: Remembering the Women's Rugby World Cup 2025 final
Rugby.summary: On 27 September 2025 - I woke up with butterflies in my stomach, and glands like conkers.
Rugby.body:
On 27 September 2025 – I woke up with butterflies in my stomach, and glands like conkers. After six cities, 10 commentaries, 11 articles, two television appearances, and countless podcasts, team base visits, press conferences, and chats with coaches and players – I was cooked. I’d not had day off in seven weeks, I had a teaspoon’s worth of adrenaline left to give, and my immune system was approaching the finish line of Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 like [you won’t regret googling this] Leo Neugebauer the end of a decathlon 1500m. I had loved every second.

The best, somehow, was still to come: all roads led to a sold-out Allianz Stadium – where the planet’s top two outfits were about to do battle. The tournament’s mantra was ‘this energy never stops’, and – that day – it escalated precociously early. Just exiting Twickenham station was a thrill: scarves hawked, cowboy hats adjusted, and handmade signs brandished. Someone, somehow, had cranked up the saturation on the Cabbage Patch pub’s mural – and totemic figures of Zoe Aldroft, Meg Jones and Marlie Packer appraised the procession rumbling towards the closing number to end all closing numbers.

Rugby.title: Olly Cracknell: 'I've got a bit of a chip on my shoulder'
Rugby.summary: Car enthusiast Olly Cracknell is revved up and raring to go after admitting being snubbed by Wales this summer left its mark on him.
Rugby.body:
Car enthusiast Olly Cracknell is revved up and raring to go after admitting being snubbed by Wales this summer left its mark on him. While Aaron Wainwright and Tommy Reffell, his back-row colleagues in Sunday’s home clash with Saracens, added to their caps tally in the Nations Championship, Cracknell was overlooked in July by head coach Steve Tandy, despite featuring a few months earlier in the Six Nations.

“I was part of the intial squad but then I wasn’t selected for the tour, so that was obviously disappointing,” said the 32-year-old, who has made 87 appearances for Leicester since joining the club in 2022.

Rugby.body:
Has one player ever been as important to the All Blacks as Cam Roigard is right now? Even the legendary Dan Carter might not be able to claim as much. Rugby.summary: The USA Women's Eagles have won three games in a row for the first time in 20 year with a performance that head coach Jack Hanratty branded as "brilliant".
Rugby.body:
The USA Women’s Eagles have won three games in a row for the first time in 20 years, with a performance that head coach Jack Hanratty branded as “brilliant”. On Saturday afternoon, the USA head coach watched his team pick up a 26-24 WXV Global Series win against Wales in Cardiff.

The victory backed up last week’s win against Ireland. Combined with their July victory over the Springbok Women in Pretoria, it means the North Americans have won three games on the bounce for the first time since 2006.

Rugby.summary: The 39-year-old head coach admitted her side were "chasing a performance", especially against the benchmark of Women's rugby.
Rugby.body:
One moment separated the Black Ferns and England at Allianz Stadium on Sunday morning, when Amy Du’Plessis’ pass found Zoe Harrison instead of a teammate in black. For 80 minutes, the two best teams in the world went toe-to-toe in front of 59,000 fans in London, but it wasn’t enough for the Kiwis as John Mitchell’s side extended their unbeaten streak to 40 matches.

Whitney Hansen’s Black Ferns led the contest 12-7 at halftime, thanks to five-pointers from Du Plessis and Ayesha Leti-I’iga, while Claudia Moloney-MacDonald opened the scoring for the home side in the 14th minute.

Rugby.body:
Upon their return to winning ways, the Springbok Women said they “were not going to be beaten” by Italy. A week ago, the world’s 10th-ranked side were left shocked by Wales in Cardiff, as Sean Lynn’s side registered a 50-19 win. South Africa returned to winning ways at the first time of asking with a 41-29 victory against the *Azzurre* in Pordenone.

The Springbok Women rode their luck at times as their 24-10 half-time lead was overturned in the second half, as converted tries from Italy’s Alyssa D’Inca and Vittoria Ostuni Minuzzi, along with a Michaela Sillari penalty, handed the hosts a narrow lead with 15 minutes remaining.

Rugby.title: Cardiff seal opening Welsh derby win over Scarlets
Rugby.summary: Cardiff triumph in the first United Rugby Championship (URC) Welsh derby of the season by beating Scarlets in Llanelli.
Rugby.body:
Cardiff triumphed in the first United Rugby Championship (URC) Welsh derby of the season by beating Scarlets in Llanelli. Tries from flanker Dan Thomas, player-of-the-match Taine Basham and replacement hooker Evan Lloyd helped seal the victory, with all three tries coming from effective attacking driving line-outs.

Scarlets scored first-half tries through centre Joe Roberts and full-back Blair Murray but could only manage a second-half penalty from Joe Hawkins. Wales centre Eddie James starred for Scarlets, but he could not inspire a home victory.

Rugby.title: England embrace growing competitiveness of women's game
Rugby.summary: England edge past New Zealand with a last-gasp try by Zoe Harrison as they embrace the growing competitiveness of women's rugby.
Rugby.body:
Winning had been the only currency known to John Mitchell's Red Roses. From his arrival midway through the 2023 WXV1 campaign to winning the Women's Rugby World Cup for the first time in 11 years, England won every single game.

However, their record 39-game run of victories was finally halted by Canada, last year's World Cup finalists, in a thrilling 26-26 draw at Sandy Park last week. Welcoming New Zealand, unbeaten under new head coach Whitney Hansen, to Allianz Stadium brought a feeling of jeopardy that had not been felt for a very long time.
Rugby.copy:
Winning had been the only currency known to John Mitchell's Red Roses. From his arrival midway through the 2023 WXV1 campaign to winning the Women's Rugby World Cup for the first time in 11 years, England won every single game.

However, their record 39-game run of victories was finally halted by Canada, last year's World Cup finalists, in a thrilling 26-26 draw at Sandy Park last week. Welcoming New Zealand, unbeaten under new head coach Whitney Hansen, to Allianz Stadium brought a feeling of jeopardy that had not been felt for a very long time.

Rugby.title: LRZ and England star ruin Courtney Lawes' PREM return
Rugby.summary: Courtney Lawes’ Sale debut ended in defeat as Bristol ran in five tries to open their Prem Rugby campaign with an entertaining 34-24 win in Salford.
Rugby.body:
Courtney Lawes’ Sale debut ended in defeat as Bristol ran in five tries to open their Prem Rugby campaign with an entertaining 34-24 win in Salford. The 37-year-old England great made his first appearance in the competition since he led Northampton to the title at Twickenham in 2024 but it was Pat Lam’s Bears who took the spoils.

After two seasons with French club Brive, Lawes has returned to England with Sale and he started in the back row as one of two debutants in the starting line-up alongside scrum-half Xavier Roe from New Zealand.

Rugby.title: Dobie stars as Glasgow beat Munster
Rugby.summary: Glasgow Warriors begin their United Rugby Championship season in fine style as an impressive second-half turnaround earns a bonus-point win over Munster at Thomond Park.
Rugby.body:
Glasgow Warriors began their United Rugby Championship season in fine style as an impressive second-half turnaround earned a bonus-point win over Munster at Thomond Park. The Irish outfit deservedly led at half-time after Ben O'Connor and Michael Milne crossed for tries either side of Jamie Dobie's score for Glasgow.

However, Glasgow grew in stature after the interval and turned the game on its head thanks to scores from Nathan McBeth, George Horne and Dobie. Franco Smith's side, who topped the URC table last season before a heartbreaking semi-final defeat by Bulls at Murrayfield, started in sluggish fashion and were punished by the hosts.

Rugby.title: Talking points: France close out a convincing victory over Canada
Rugby.summary: France defeated Canada in a commanding 21-5 victory in the WXV Global Series at the Stade Marcel-Deflandre in La Rochelle.
Rugby.body:
France defeated Canada in a commanding 21-5 victory in the WXV Global Series at the Stade Marcel-Deflandre in La Rochelle. Les Bleues came into this contest after claiming a 29-26 victory over Australia last weekend. They had to recover from a difficult start against the Wallaroos and scored late to secure the win.

After losing 28-14 to New Zealand in their opening fixture, France looked to build on that comeback and produce a more controlled performance against Canada. Kevin Rouet’s side came into the game unbeaten in the opening two rounds. They began their campaign with a 64-26 win over Scotland before holding England to a 26-26 draw last weekend in a repeat of the 2025 Women’s Rugby World Cup Final. That result demonstrated their ability to match England’s intensity and would have given them plenty of confidence heading to France.

Rugby.summary: Head coach Sean Lynn is still seeing the positives despite Wales' narrow WXV defeat to USA.
Rugby.body:
Head coach Sean Lynn says he is still seeing the positives despite Wales' narrow WXV defeat to USA. Wales had gone into the game full of confidence after their eight-try mauling of South Africa, but failed to produce a repeat performance in front of the Cardiff Arms Park faithful.

The first half was encouraging enough, with Wales clawing back a 14-point deficit, but hopes of a second-half resurgence were short-lived amid a string of individual errors that allowed The Eagles to emerge 26-24 winners.

Rugby.summary: Australia battled back from 10-5 down at half-time to defeat Scotland 30-10 in WXV Global Series action at Hive Stadium in Edinburgh on Saturday.
Rugby.body:
Australia battled back from 10-5 down at half-time to defeat Scotland 30-10 in WXV Global Series action at Hive Stadium in Edinburgh on Saturday. In front of a crowd of 3,191, the Wallaroos won their first game since March and halted a run of six defeats in a row.

For Scotland, this was a seventh defeat in a row. They played well in the first half, but did not put enough points on the board when on top and they were overawed in the second period here.

Rugby.title: England return to winning ways after thrilling finish against New Zealand
Rugby.summary: .England were spared a second successive draw after Zoe Harrison plundered an overtime try to break New Zealand’s hearts in a 26-19 victory at Allianz Stadium.
Rugby.body:
England were spared a second successive draw after Zoe Harrison plundered an overtime try to break New Zealand’s hearts in a 26-19 victory at Allianz Stadium. A week after their 39-Test winning streak came to an end with a 26-26 stalemate against Canada, the world champions needed Harrison’s opportunism in the 82nd minute to topple another of their great rivals.

It was cruel on the Black Ferns, who bravely attacked from close to their own line in a high-risk, high-reward strategy designed to turn a draw into a last-gasp triumph. But it ultimately backfired as their intent to go wide with a long pass was read by Harrison, who picked off the intercept before converting to finish the afternoon with an 11-point haul that included three conversions.

Rugby.body:
Gloucester head coach George Skivington praised the impact his big-name new signings have already made after they swept aside Exeter Chiefs 45-24 at Sandy Park. New skipper and hooker Dewi Lake scored two tries, while his Wales international team-mate Jac Morgan and South African lock Jean Kleyn also made big contributions to the impressive bonus-point victory.

Skivington said: “The result is great, but what we saw in character, particularly in some of those defensive sets from the boys, is a good snapshot of what we have asked them to go after this year.

Rugby.title: Lions player ratings vs Leinster | URC 2026/27
Rugby.summary: Lions player ratings: The Lions won't care that Leinster enjoyed plenty of possession at Ellis Park because Ivan van Rooyen's side were far more ruthless when it mattered.
Rugby.body:
Lions player ratings: The Lions won’t care that Leinster enjoyed plenty of possession at Ellis Park because Ivan van Rooyen’s side were far more ruthless when it mattered. While the visitors played with ambition and frequently moved the ball through the hands, the Lions punished errors, dominated key scrum exchanges and found a way to win despite seeing less of the ball. Erich Cronje was their chief tormentor out wide, while Sebastian Lombard, Siba Mahashe and the pack laid the physical foundations for an opening-round URC victory in Johannesburg.

A composed display from the back. Kicked well from hand throughout and produced several important clearances under pressure. His break and assist helped create Cronje’s second try, while he also sliced through the defence himself early in the second half.

Scotland suffered a third successive defeat in the WXV Global Series as clinical Australia proved too strong in Edinburgh. Rugby.title: Talking points: Hat-trick hero Tafuna secures victory over Wales
Rugby.summary: The USA Women’s Eagles made it two wins from two in Europe after edging Wales 26-24 in a feisty contest at Cardiff Arms Park.
Rugby.body:
The USA Women’s Eagles made it two wins from two in Europe after edging Wales 26-24 in a feisty contest at Cardiff Arms Park. The visitors flew out of the blocks as their forwards patiently worked through the phases before last week’s player of the match Freda Tafuna went crashing under the posts for the first try of the game.

Bella Vogel added the extras with ease and the Eagles were 7-0 up early on. It was a fiery start to say the least, with referee Amber McLachlan speaking to the captains after some heated words were exchanged between the sides, but the USA continued to apply huge pressure and Tafuna crossed once again, with co-captain Georgie Perris-Redding helping to drive her on.

Rugby.title: New recruits shine as Gloucester batter illness-hit Exeter Chiefs
Rugby.summary: New-look Gloucester got their season off to a cracking start with an emphatic 45-24 bonus-point victory over last season’s beaten Prem finalists Exeter at Sandy Park.
Rugby.body:
New-look Gloucester got their season off to a cracking start with an emphatic 45-24 bonus-point victory over last season’s beaten Prem finalists Exeter at Sandy Park. Inspired by impressive summer arrivals Dewi Lake, Jac Morgan and Jean Kleyn, it was Gloucester’s first league win on Devon soil since 2015.

Exeter, ravaged by illness on top of the squad absences they already had, looked out of sorts for large parts of the game and only in the closing stages once the outcome was beyond doubt, did they look more like their usual selves.

Rugby.summary: Zoe Harrison saved England’s 40-game unbeaten game streak with an intercept try at the death against New Zealand in front of 59,871 fans at Allianz Stadium.
Rugby.body:
Zoe Harrison saved England’s 40-game unbeaten game streak with an intercept try at the death against New Zealand in front of 59,871 fans at Allianz Stadium. When Harrison stepped up to take a penalty in the 80th minute from just inside the halfway in a courageous go-for-broke moment, the stadium held their breadth in anticipation.

But the kick fell short and England fans thought the game with it, until floated to the wing by New Zealand was picked off by Harrison from nowhere, this time making sure to nail the conversion on the full-time whistle 26-19.

Rugby.body:
Gloucester delivered an outstanding performance on the first weekend of the new Prem season to stun Exeter Chiefs at Sandy Park. The Cherry and Whites only once won on the road last term as they finished eighth, but they matched that immediately with this superb showing.

Summer arrival, and new captain and Wales skipper, Dewi Lake led the way with two of their seven tries. Winger Ben Loader helped himself to two, while Seb Atkinson, a fine solo effort from Will Joseph and a debut try from Junior Denny completed their try haul.
