Rugby.title: Exeter Chiefs player ratings vs Gloucester | 2026/27 Gallagher PREM
Rugby.summary: Exeter Chiefs player ratings: Exeter Chiefs were handed a difficult start to their Gallagher PREM campaign as Gloucester left Sandy Park with an emphatic 45-24 victory.
Rugby.body:
Exeter Chiefs player ratings: Exeter Chiefs were handed a difficult start to their Gallagher PREM campaign as Gloucester left Sandy Park with an emphatic 45-24 victory. There were plenty of encouraging individual performances from the Chiefs, particularly from an explosive back-row of Ethan Roots, Kane James and Greg Fisilau, but Gloucester continually found ways through the home defence. Exeter remained dangerous with ball in hand and scored four tries of their own, though they were ultimately unable to contain their visitors as the contest opened up.

A relatively quiet afternoon at the back. Made 27 metres from four carries but endured some difficult defensive moments, missing three tackles before being withdrawn after 63 minutes.

Rugby.summary: Zoe Harrison scores last-gasp try as England defeat New Zealand at Allianz Stadium to avoid a second successive draw in the WXV Global Series.
Rugby.body:
Zoe Harrison scored a last-gasp try as England defeated New Zealand at Allianz Stadium to avoid a second successive draw in the WXV Global Series. With the scores level at 19-19 in the 81st minute and having missed a penalty moments earlier, Harrison intercepted a pass as the Black Ferns tried to counter-attack, the fly-half diving over the line and piled up on by celebrating team-mates.

The world champions' record 39-game winning run came to an end last weekend in the 26-26 draw with Canada, but this week they were able to find a dramatic path to victory, much to the delight of the 59,871 crowd.

Rugby.summary: Ospreys well beaten by Sharks in United Rugby Championship opener but earn consolation four-try bonus.
Rugby.body:
Ospreys suffered an opening weekend United Rugby Championship (URC) defeat in South Africa for the second successive season after being overpowered by Sharks. Mark Jones' men were comprehensively beaten in Durban but, just as they did when losing at Bulls in 2025, Ospreys at least have the consolation of a four-try bonus.

Sharks led 28-14 at half-time thanks to tries by Nick Hatton, Manu Tshituka, Luan Giliomee and Lili Bester. Ospreys stayed in the contest with scores by Luke Morgan and Sam Parry, then were right back in it when former Australia captain Liam Wright went through a gaping hole on his debut.

Rugby.summary: Wales' resurgence suffers a blow with USA edging an entertaining WXV contest at Cardiff Arms Park.
Rugby.body:
Wales' resurgence suffered a disappointing blow with USA edging an entertaining WXV contest at Cardiff Arms Park. Number eight Freda Tafuna, a standout player in USA's victory over Ireland last week, bagged a hat-trick as the error-strewn hosts struggled to find the fluidity that saw them cruise past South Africa.

Erica Coulibaly also crossed for the visitors, while Wales stayed in the fight with scores from Keira Bevan, Kelsey Jones, Sisilia Tuipulotu and Alex Callender. But the Eagles dominated the second-half, once again proving they are rising force in the women's game and living up to their status as a top-six side.

Rugby.summary: South Africa held on against Italy to claim a nail-biting 41-29 victory in the WXV Global Series at Stadio Omero Tognon.
Rugby.body:
South Africa held on against Italy to claim a nail-biting 41-29 victory in the WXV Global Series at Stadio Omero Tognon. The Springbok Women looked firmly in control after racing into a 24-12 half-time lead, but Italy produced a brilliant second half fightback to turn the game on its head.

The Azzurre briefly moved 29-27 ahead with 20 minutes remaining before South Africa regained control late on. Anushka Groenewald scored twice in the first half, alongside Byrhandre Dolf and Maria Tshiremba, while Alyssa D’Inca and Vittoria Vecchini kept Italy within touching distance at the break.

Rugby.title: Leinster edged out by Lions despite Gunne treble
Rugby.summary: URC champions Leinster are edged out 27-26 by the Lions in their season opener despite Fintan Gunne's first-half hat-trick of tries.
Rugby.body:
Leinster were edged out 27-26 by the Lions in their opening United Rugby Championship game at Ellis Park on Saturday. The Irish province tasted defeat despite a hat-trick of tries by Fintan Gunne in the first half, although a late touchdown by Stephen Smyth ensured they left Johannesburg with a bonus point.

Scrum-half Gunne squeezed through the Lions defence after six minutes for the opening score but Erich Cronje crossed for the hosts soon after, Chris Smith kicking the conversion.

Rugby.title: Weakened Leinster stumble at start of URC title defence in South Africa
Rugby.summary: Leinster slipped to a 27-26 defeat against the Lions in their United Rugby Championship opener, despite Fintan Gunne scoring a first-half hat-trick.
Rugby.body:
Leinster slipped to a 27-26 defeat against the Lions in their United Rugby Championship opener, despite Fintan Gunne scoring a first-half hat-trick. Gunne opened the scoring for the defending champions just six minutes in after squeezing through the Lions’ defence, but Caspar Gabriel was unable to convert and the hosts soon replied when Erich Cronje touched down and Chris Smith added the extras.

Smith extended their advantage from the tee with a penalty, but Leinster drew level shortly afterwards as Josh Ericson broke through the home defence before offloading to Gunne, who raced over for his second try which Gabriel was able to convert.

Rugby.title: Leinster player ratings vs Lions | URC 2026/27
Rugby.summary: Leinster player ratings: With a few exceptions, this was a Leinster B side, but they arrived at Ellis Park with a clear intent to upset the hosts, albeit in front of a pretty poor crowd.
Rugby.body:
Leinster player ratings: With a few exceptions, this was a Leinster B side, but they arrived at Ellis Park with a clear intent to upset the hosts, albeit in front of a pretty poor crowd. Leinster were brave, ambitious and willing to move the ball, but they ultimately made too many errors with ball in hand and the Lions punished them despite enjoying far less possession for large spells.

An appalling scrum once again hurt Leinster’s efforts repeatedly and remains a massive headache for Leo Cullen, particularly when the pressure started to mount in the second half.

Rugby.title: Killers of Los Pumas star Aramburu sentenced in France
Rugby.summary: The two men convicted over the killing of former Argentina international Federico Martín Aramburu have been sentenced by a court in Paris.
Rugby.body:
The two men convicted over the killing of former Argentina international Federico Martín Aramburu have been sentenced by a court in Paris. Loïk Le Priol, 32, was jailed for 26 years after being found guilty of murdering Aramburu, while Romain Bouvier, 35, received a 19-year prison sentence after being convicted of attempted murder.

Aramburu, who won 22 caps for Argentina and spent much of his club career in France with Biarritz, was shot dead in Paris in March 2022 after an altercation outside a bar in the city’s Saint-Germain district. He was 42.

Rugby.title: Fissler Confidential: England star opens talks as PREM club go to market
Rugby.summary: England international inside centre Max Ojomoh has opened talks with former Gallagher PREM champions Bath about extending his deal, which runs out at the end of the season.
Rugby.body:
England international inside centre Max Ojomoh has opened talks with former Gallagher PREM champions Bath about extending his deal, which runs out at the end of the season. Ojomoh, 26, scored a try in his only England appearance against Argentina last season and has an international record of two tries in two games. He entered the final year of his contract in July, but Bath have started talks early.

He has been a target for Leicester Tigers in the past but has always opted to stay at the Rec, and Bath are hoping to wrap up talks in the next few weeks once again. Fijian Olympic gold medallist Iosefo Masi, who was in the final year of his contract with Top 14 outfit Lyon, has put pen to paper on a two-year extension and will stay at the Stade de Gerland until 2029.

Rugby.title: Mack may be back but Stormers blow Connacht away in Galway
Rugby.summary: Connacht let a second-half lead slip in their opening match in Galway as Stormers hit back with two late tries to seal the South African side a 29-15 win.
Rugby.body:
Connacht let a second-half lead slip in their opening match in Galway as Stormers hit back with two late tries to seal the South African side a 29-15 win. Stormers punished Connacht for their sloppy opening, with Jurie Matthee’s early penalty and full-back Warrick Gelent’s superb converted try giving the visitors a 10-0 lead.

Connacht finished the first half strongly and five minutes before the interval, wing Mack Hansen followed up Cathal Forde’s barnstorming run to dive over for a converted score.

Rugby.title: Wallabies dealt big injury blow on eve of Springboks showdown
Rugby.summary: The Wallabies have suffered a big loss on the eve of Sunday’s clash against the two-time defending world champion Springboks in Perth.
Rugby.body:
The Wallabies have suffered a big loss on the eve of Sunday’s clash against the two-time defending world champion Springboks in Perth, with lineout caller and in-form lock Josh Canham ruled out with a minor hamstring strain.

Canham hadn’t started a match in Wallaby gold before the Nations Championship Test in July, but the second-rower has quickly emerged as a core member of the side. The 25-year-old has featured in six Tests this season, and was set for another appearance this weekend.

Rugby.summary: The 2024 and 2025 New Zealand Under-20s first-five or fullback is already a regular starter for Auckland in the NPC. As of September 24, he has played 24 of Auckland’s last 28 games.

Rico Simpson is adamant that the best form of defence is attack. The 2024 and 2025 New Zealand Under-20s first-five or fullback is already a regular starter for Auckland in the NPC. As of September 24, he has played 24 of Auckland’s last 28 games.

Rugby.title: Josh Goodhue on how the Ranfurly Shield has rallied the Northland region
Rugby.summary: The Log o’ Wood has been everywhere from Whangarei to Cape Reinga. It was successfully defended on August 30 against Tasman 20-10 at a sold-out Semenoff Stadium and again on September 12 against Waikato 34-17.
Rugby.body:
It’s been a whirlwind month for Northland since their 36-12 crushing of Canterbury in Christchurch on August 19 to win the Ranfurly Shield for the first time since 1979. The Log o’ Wood has been everywhere from Whangarei to Cape Reinga. It was successfully defended on August 30 against Tasman 20-10 at a sold-out Semenoff Stadium and again on September 12 against Waikato 34-17.

Josh Goodhue, 31, has played 71 matches for the Taniwha. The rugged lock from Kawakawa in the Bay of Islands is one of three brothers, with Jack (All Black) and Cameron the others, to have played for Northland. Dad Bernard is a life member of Northland rugby and, with another brother Axel, they’re stalwarts of the Kawakawa rugby club.

Rugby.title: Edinburgh raid Belfast after holding off Ulster fightback
Rugby.summary: Edinburgh held off a late fightback from Ulster to secure an opening-day 34-29 win in the United Rugby Championship at Affidea Stadium.
Rugby.body:
Edinburgh held off a late fightback from Ulster to secure an opening-day 34-29 win in the United Rugby Championship at Affidea Stadium. The visitors led 20-5 at half-time and 34-5 after 49 minutes and although Ulster came roaring back with three second-half tries and a late penalty from Jack Murphy to lift them to within five points, it was not enough.

Freddy Douglas’ converted opening touchdown and James Grayson’s penalty gave Edinburgh a 10-0 lead before Mikey Lowry went over for Ulster’s first score. But another Grayson penalty and a second converted Edinburgh try from Malelili Satala put the Scottish side 20-5 ahead at the break.

Rugby.title: Ulster fightback comes up short in loss to Edinburgh
Rugby.summary: Ulster's thrilling second-half comeback comes up short as Edinburgh leave Belfast with a 34-29 win in the opening game of the United Rugby Championship.
Rugby.body:
Ulster's thrilling second-half comeback came up short as Edinburgh left Belfast with a 34-29 win in the opening game of the United Rugby Championship. In a pulsating start to the new season, the Scottish side played Ulster off the pitch in the first 55 minutes as they built what looked like an unassailable 34-5 lead.

Tries came from Freddy Douglas, Malelili Satala, Hector Patterson and Piers O’Conor, with James Grayson converting them all and adding two penalties. Only Michael Lowry’s try troubled the scorers for Ulster.

Rugby.title: Carreras magic lights up Bath win over Harlequins
Rugby.summary: A terrific try from full-back Santiago Carreras is the highlight of Bath's Prem opening night bonus-point victory over Harlequins.
Rugby.body:
A terrific try from full-back Santiago Carreras was the highlight of Bath's opening night 33-17 bonus-point victory over Harlequins. The Argentina international intercepted a Tyrone Green pass with his boot, kicking the ball into the air before collecting it one-handed before it went out of play and smoothly accelerating away to score under the posts in a real moment of magic.

Dan du Preez, Joe Cokanasiga and Dan Frost added first-half tries for Bath who led 28-10 at the break, with Will Porter and Chandler Cunningham-South replying for Quins. Pedro Delgado reduced the gap to 11 points early in the second half but Ewan Richards' late try ensured it would be Bath who started the new season with a win.

Rugby.title: Gareth Gilbert: Netherlands have shown ‘a lot of potential’ at WXV
Rugby.summary: Outgoing Netherlands head coach Gareth Gilbert believes his team's efforts at WXV Global Series Challenger have set the team up for long-term success.
Rugby.body:
Outgoing Netherlands head coach Gareth Gilbert believes his team’s efforts at the WXV Global Series Challenger have set the team up for long-term success. This weekend, the Oranje face the Fijiana in a winner-takes-all clash at Kai Tak Youth Sports Ground. The Netherlands have beaten Samoa and Brazil in their first two matches of the tournament, while the Pacific Islanders have recorded wins over Spain and Hong Kong China.

Those results have lifted the Netherlands two places in the World Rugby rankings to 15th, with the likes of Kika Mulling making an impact. “These three weeks have shown that there’s a lot of potential in the Dutch game,” Gilbert told reporters this week. “I think we’ll get more opportunities, which is justified.

Rugby.title: Wales out to prove they are no one-hit wonder
Rugby.summary: Wales and USA will both be looking to back up impressive WXV opening round victories when they go head-to-head at Cardiff Arms Park on Saturday.
Rugby.body:
Resurgent, inspired, unrecognisable, brave - pick one. Each describes Wales' performance against South Africa in their WXV opener. Sean Lynn's side scored eight tries against one of the rising forces in women's rugby in one of the best displays of their professional era.

But they know they cannot afford to bask in glory. Wales must now prove they are more than a one-hit wonder when they return to Cardiff Arms Park on Saturday. The next - and even bigger - challenge is USA, who, like the Springboks, have rocketed up the world rankings and are now a top six team.

Rugby.title: Rugby à 7: where to train in Paris and the Ile-de-France region, and in which clubs?
Rugby.summary: Rugby à 7: where to train in Paris and the Ile-de-France region, and in which clubs? Sortir à Paris
Rugby.body:
Founded in 1848 in the English town of Rugby, rugby is among the sports that enjoy the greatest popularity in France. And there’s a good reason: the country hosts a wealth of competitions, from the Top 14 and the Pro D2 to the Six Nations Championship... Less popular than rugby union, rugby sevens is the second-most played form of the sport in France, with rules that differ from those of traditional rugby union.

Games are therefore shorter (just 14 minutes of play versus 80 minutes in 15-a-side rugby), split into two 40-minute halves. In rugby sevens, matches are also more intense, with fewer players on a field of the same size, which means you need very different kinds of athletes.

Rugby.title: ‘Brendan takes things very emotionally, very personally. It’s part of his super power’
Rugby.summary: The colourful South African’s decision to return for a second stint as Saracens director of rugby triggers a panorama of possibilities.
Rugby.body:
Brendan Venter’s return to the English rugby frontline this season carries with it the prospect of creativity and controversy in equal measure. The colourful South African’s decision to leave his Cape Town medical practice and return for a second stint as Saracens director of rugby triggers a panorama of possibilities.

On the one hand Venter is one of the game’s sharpest minds. As Italy’s defence coach in 2017, he was the architect of ‘The Fox’ tactic which magically erased the offside line and, for a half at least, until a baffled England worked out how to play against it, gave a vastly inferior side parity at Twickenham.

Rugby.summary: The Wallaroos or Scotland could end the weekend ranked sixth in the World Rugby rankings when the latest weekend of WXV Global Series fixtures conclude.
Rugby.body:
The Wallaroos or Scotland could end the weekend ranked sixth in the World Rugby rankings when the latest weekend of WXV Global Series fixtures concludes. Which team moves up in the rankings will be determined by the winner of the two teams’ meeting in Edinburgh on Saturday. It is the first time the two teams have met on Scottish soil.

There is even potential for the Wallaroos to move to fifth and equal their highest-ever position in the rankings if Ireland lose to Japan. England will not lose top spot in the World Rugby rankings, although their lead can be cut to 0.75 points if the Black Ferns win by 15 points or more at Allianz Stadium.

Rugby.title: Answering John Mitchell’s question: Bryony Field on her England breakthrough
Rugby.summary: Driving home from training a couple of weeks ago, after learning that she had been selected to play for England for the first time, Bryony Field’s mind was understandably all over the place when she ended up in a relatable situation.
Rugby.body:
Driving home from training a couple of weeks ago, after learning that she had been selected to play for England for the first time, Bryony Field’s mind was understandably all over the place when she ended up in a relatable situation.

“I actually crashed my car on the way home,” Field explains. “Obviously I was buzzing, and my mind was a little bit aloof. And on the M25 I rammed into the back of someone. I got home from camp that day and I thought, ‘what on earth has just happened?’”

Rugby.title: ‘He has an aura’: Why Shaun Edwards joined the Red Roses
Rugby.summary: Shaun Edwards' arrival in Red Roses camp had been several weeks in the making.
Rugby.body:
Shaun Edwards’ arrival in Red Roses camp had been several weeks in the making. Freshly released from his commitments with France after six years working with Fabien Galthie’s team – a stint that yielded a Guinness Six Nations Grand Slam and back-to-back Championship victories – the 59-year-old was a free agent for the first time in over four decades.

Those Six Nations successes only scratch the surface of Edwards’ career. As a player he captained Wigan Warriors in their most famous era and as a coach enjoyed domestic and European success with Wasps, before a 12-year stay as Wales defence coach. Given that pedigree, you would have to think he had plenty of suitors.

Rugby.title: R360 rebel series given ultimatum on overdue accounts
Rugby.summary: The company behind R360, the controversial all-star rugby start-up, has been ordered to publish overdue accounts or face being dissolved.
Rugby.body:
The company behind R360, the controversial all-star rugby start-up, has been ordered to publish overdue accounts or face being dissolved. R360 originally had a launch date of October 2026, but has postponed its inaugural edition until 2028 after a concerted move against it by eight leading Test nations and the British and Irish Lions.

AOTG Sport was scheduled to file accounts with Companies House in July, covering a period up to the end of December 2025. Earlier this week, it was served with a strike-off notice,, external giving two months to hand over the overdue paperwork or be put out of business.

Rugby.title: Justine Pelletier column: 'I understand why we had to kick the ball out'
Rugby.summary: I should probably answer the question everyone is wondering. Yes, I thought we could beat the Red Roses.
Rugby.body:
I should probably answer the question everyone is wondering. Yes, I thought we could beat the Red Roses. But I also understand why we had to kick the ball out. It had been 20 minutes of defending, which, as it happens, preceded my time on the pitch at Sandy Park. Sometimes a draw is a good enough ending for what we are trying to do and where we are trying to go. It felt like a good fight. The score was going back and forth between us leading to an undefined winner. I think we showed great dominance in that game.

DaLeaka Menin was absolutely relentless. You do not often see a prop go from start to finish. It was little wonder that she got Player of the Match and then Player of the Week.

Rugby.summary: England scrum-half Natasha Hunt says it is no longer possible to satisfy fans' post-match requests for selfies and autographs, given the Red Roses' success and growth.
Rugby.body:
England scrum-half Natasha Hunt says it is no longer possible to satisfy fans' post-match requests for selfies and autographs, given the Red Roses' success and growth over the past decade.

Hunt, 37, made her England debut in 2011, when the team were regularly playing in front of three-figure crowds. Even in 2019, an attendance of 4,674 at the Women's Six Nations game against France set a new record for a standalone Red Roses game away from a Rugby World Cup.

Rugby.summary: Ulster legend Stephen Ferris says that the pressure is on Richie Murphy because they cannot afford to miss out on the United Rugby Championship play-offs for a third successive season.
Rugby.body:

The former Ireland and Lions flanker points out that Ulster need to be playing in the Champions Cup, but that won’t happen unless Murphy can guide them to a top eight finish. Last season they finished two points adrift of the play-off places after Ferris says they put all their eggs in one basket, reaching the Challenge Cup Final only to lose to Montpellier in Bilbao.

Rugby.title: Ex-Boks coach insists South Africa are thin in one key area
Rugby.summary: Former Springboks assistant coach Gary Gold has recent first-hand experience of facing Australia, as defence coach of Japan, who the Wallabies met in back-to-back Tests in August.
Rugby.body:
Former Springboks assistant coach Gary Gold has heralded the extraordinary depth of talent built up by Rassie Erasmus since they won the last Rugby World Cup. Writing in an article on his website, Gold is full of admiration for how Erasmus has blooded players over time to the point now where they are at least five-deep in every position bar one.

While Gold believes there are nine locks who could do an equally good job, for example, his only concern is at fly-half, where there is a three-way fight for the No.10 jersey between Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu, double World Cup winner Handre Pollard and Manie Libbok.

Rugby.title: Mick Cleary: 'You win nowt without proper team spirit, no matter how many high-performing individuals you have in the ranks.'
Rugby.summary: Still a tad light at ten teams, there's no doubt Prem Rugby is gathering momentum as the season starts off with a bang...
Rugby.body:
It was 40 years ago today, as the song almost goes, that yours truly first started covering what used to be known as first-class rugby, merit tables and all that, the forerunner of proper leagues and one of the eventual trigger points for the game turning pro in the mid-nineties. Full-blooded (and occasionally filthy) as the games were back then there was still an amateur feel to so much of it. How could it not be when the phone number for the RFU at Twickenham was still ex-directory and the players were clocking on for work on Monday mornings?

No comparison then to the all-singing, all-dancing PREM which begins on Friday evening with two league games – why two..why not go for a single big bang opener with a showdown between the last two winners, Northampton and Bath – and several months of club action to come? Well, the club game is obviously a significantly bigger draw card for spectators, attendances which help pay the bills, but there are certain truths that are remarkably similar. Firstly, there was a trenchant article in Rugby World magazine in autumn 1986 entitled ‘The Decline of British Back Play,’ written by some bloke with the name of Stephen Jones (whatever happened to him?) while out on the field itself Bath were girding their loins to begin their run of dominance on the English domestic scene in much the manner that their latter-day equivalents, Bath Rugby itself or Northampton Saints, will have designs on replicating.

Rugby.title: ‘Best in the world’: Brown ready for backyard battle in Ultimate Sevens finale
Rugby.summary: One of England’s most decorated sevens players Abbie Brown has experienced first hand the incredible athletic feats sevens rugby players can accomplish.
Rugby.body:
One of England’s most decorated sevens players Abbie Brown has experienced first hand the incredible athletic feats sevens rugby players can accomplish. As the Ultimates Sevens tournament is set to begin at Brentford Community Stadium in London on Thursday, the Team GB star, Commonwealth Games medalist and captain of the Albion Athletic women’s team is hoping the tournament can show how much potential the format has outside of the SVNS Series circuit.

Athletic currently sit at the bottom of the table coming into the final round – but with the unique format of Ultimate Sevens seeing a winner-takes-all format in Brentford, Brown’s side is more than capable of coming home late with a wet sail to win.

Rugby.title: Christie puts no limits on Newcastle ambition
Rugby.summary: Newcastle Red Bulls captain Tom Christie is excited as the new-look team take a step into the unknown in The Prem this season.
Rugby.body:
Tom Christie laughs at the suggestion he is now one of the veterans in the Newcastle Red Bulls squad. Rugby.title: 'Nothing was going to hold me back': Orphaned at 12, Siphosethu Mnebelele has defied the odds
Rugby.summary: The hooker lost both parents in a devastating six-month period before he'd started high school. Eight years on, he has become one of the hottest properties in South African rugby.
Rugby.body:
Nosipho Mnebelele only watched her son play one rugby match. She didn’t care for the sport initially. Despite her boy’s prodigious size, she worried he would get hurt. She was suspicious of any activity which upset his focus or dragged him away from his schoolwork. A single parent in South Africa’s harsh and troubled gold mining country, her concerns were not unfounded.

Siphosethu Mnebelele was her youngest child. He has endured, conquered and achieved more in his 20 years on this planet than most encounter in three lifetimes. The unfathomable loss of both parents and a grandparent in a six-month period before he’d hit his teens. The sense-scrambling road from a West Rand township to one of the most prestigious schools in South Africa, his anointing as captain at the country’s great Craven Week talent show, back-to-back Junior World Championship crowns, the latter as skipper, invitations to Rassie Erasmus’ Springbok squad and now, this Saturday, a URC debut among the Sharks Galacticos. A battalion of relatives, coaches and teachers helped the hooker on his way; seeing the talent and drive in a boy who was forced to leave adolescence behind for the sake of his family.

Rugby.title: 'I want to be gold medal ready': Sarah Hirini returns with sights set on a fourth Olympics
Rugby.summary: Sarah Hirini intends to be “gold medal” ready as she commits to a fourth Olympic campaign with the Black Ferns Sevens.
Rugby.body:
Sarah Hirini intends to be “gold medal” ready as she commits to a fourth Olympic campaign with the Black Ferns Sevens. The legendary leader, who has won everything there is to win in the sport including captaining New Zealand to two golds and one silver medal, has signed a new two-year contract with New Zealand Rugby, taking her through to the LA Olympics.

The deal will make her the longest serving professionally contracted female player in New Zealand rugby history. Having signed her first contract in 2012, by the time this one ends in 2028 she’ll have been in the Black Ferns Sevens for more than half her life. This time around she’ll be doing it with baby Masaru in tow. Born in May while Hirini and her husband Conor were living in Japan, his name means “victory”.

Rugby.title: Bears pair Staddon and Heward suffer ACL injuries
Rugby.summary: Bristol Bears pair Ethan Staddon and Noah Heward suffer ACL injuries while Kalaveti Ravouvou is out for 12 weeks with a knee injury.
Rugby.body:
New Bristol Bears signing Ethan Staddon and back Noah Heward have both suffered anterior cruciate ligament injuries and face long spells on the sidelines. Staddon was Bristol's most high-profile signing this summer, with the versatile back-row forward making the move from neighbours Bath.

However he has already undergone surgery, as has Heward, who went off five minutes into the team's Prem Rugby Cup loss to Exeter two weeks ago. Centre Kalaveti Ravouvou is also unavailable for around 12 weeks after picking up a knee injury while on international duty with Fiji, and is unlikely to feature until after the November international break.

Rugby.summary: Head coach Geoff Parling says Leicester Tigers need to keep "evolving" in their constant pursuit of silverware.
Rugby.body:
Head coach Geoff Parling says Leicester Tigers need to keep "evolving" in their constant pursuit of silverware. The East Midlands club finished fourth in the Prem table and were beaten in the semi-finals of the competition in Parling's first season in charge last term.

Tigers did, however, win the Prem Cup and reached the last 16 of the European Champions Cup – where they were beaten 64-14 by eventually title winners Bordeaux Begles. Leicester start their league campaign against Saracens on Sunday, and while Parling said this season's aims had "not been discussed" he admits the aspirations of English rugby's most decorated side is inescapable.

Rugby.summary: A case could be made for all four South African teams reaching the play-offs this season, but each has points to prove with RWC places on the line.
Rugby.body:
One URC title in five completed seasons is a poor return for four teams that provide the domestic spine of the Springboks and have occupied six of the competition’s 10 final places.

The Stormers won the inaugural title in 2022. Since then, South African sides have reached four successive finals and lost them all. The Bulls have been runners-up in the last three, twice against Leinster and once against Glasgow. South Africa has been the URC’s most reliable finalist and its least successful champion.

Rugby.body:
Former Welsh first minister Carwyn Jones is to join Scarlets' board during a season in which their long-term future is under threat. Jones served as Wales' top politician between 2009 and 2018 and has since become a peer with the title Lord Jones of Penybont.

Born in Swansea, Jones attended Aberystwyth University, where he played rugby, before serving as a member of the Senedd for Bridgend for more than 20 years. Under Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) plans, Scarlets and Swansea-based Ospreys are rivals to remain as one of a three-team professional tier in Wales beyond 2028.

Rugby.summary: The trial concerning the murder of former Pumas international Federico Martín Aramburú, who was fatally shot on March 19, 2022, has reached a new stage...
Rugby.body:
The trial concerning the killing of former Pumas international Federico Martín Aramburú, who was fatally shot on March 19, 2022, has reached a new stage, with the attorney general in charge of the case seeking sentences of 27 and 20 years for the two defendants.

Philippe Courroye, the lead prosecutor in the case, is seeking convictions that would see Loïk Le Priol and Romain Bouvier behind bars, accusing both men of carrying out a premeditated killing.

Rugby.title: Glasgow Warriors pick 11 Scotland internationals for trip to Munster
Rugby.summary: Glasgow have selected a strong team featuring 11 Scotland internationals for their opening United Rugby Championship against Munster at Thomond Park on Saturday.
Rugby.body:
Glasgow Warriors have selected a strong team featuring 11 Scotland internationals for their opening United Rugby Championship against Munster at Thomond Park on Saturday. Hooker Gregor Hiddleston, who won his first three Test caps in the Scots’ opening Nations Championship fixtures in July, starts in the front row along with tighthead Murphy Walker, with Gregor Brown and Max Williamson packing down at lock.

Rory Darge and Matt Fagerson feature in the back row, the latter reverting from blindside to his former No.8 role after the departure of Jack Dempsey to Japan. The back three features Kyle Rowe and Jamie Dobie – making his 100th Warriors appearance – on the wings alongside soon-to-be-Scottish-qualified full-back Josh McKay, with captain Stafford McDowall and Ollie Smith teaming up at centre and George Horne starting at scrum-half alongside Dan Lancaster at No.10.

Rugby.title: McLachlan and Wills return to face Australia
Rugby.summary: Rachel McLachlan and Evie Wills return from injury to start for Scotland against Australia in their final home match of the WXV Series on Saturday.
Rugby.body:
Rachel McLachlan and Evie Wills return from injury to start for Scotland against Australia in their final home match of the WXV Series on Saturday. Sarah Bonar and Hannah Ramsay also come into the starting line-up as interim head coach Dave Butcher makes four changes following the 66-14 defeat by New Zealand.

Butcher believes facing Canada and New Zealand has helped the development of his team despite suffering two heavy defeats. "Coming out of two really, really hard games, the feeling is that we got stress tested a lot in those games, which has allowed us to accelerate what we need to do a little bit more, rather than playing a game where we're not too sure whether that will work against the world's best," he said.

Rugby.title: Scotland and Edinburgh suffer brutal Darcy Graham blow on eve of season
Rugby.summary: Edinburgh wing Darcy Graham will miss at least the first three months of the season including Scotland’s Nations Championship campaign in November after suffering a “freakish” injury on the eve of the new campaign.
Rugby.body:
Edinburgh wing Darcy Graham will miss at least the first three months of the season including Scotland’s Nations Championship campaign in November after suffering a “freakish” injury on the eve of the new campaign.

The 29-year-old flyer suffered a “contusion on his bicep” during Edinburgh’s pre-season friendly at Harlequins last Friday, his first game of the season. A subsequent MRI scan revealed Graham has ruptured a bicep muscle in his arm and is likely to be sidelined until Christmas.

Rugby.title: Injury rules Graham out of Scotland's autumn Tests
Rugby.summary: Scotland's record try-scorer Darcy Graham is to miss the autumn internationals against New Zealand, Australia and Japan with a ruptured bicep.
Rugby.body:
Scotland's record try-scorer Darcy Graham is to miss the autumn internationals with a bicep injury. The 29-year-old Edinburgh winger has 38 tries from his 57 caps but will not have the chance to add to that tally in home Tests against New Zealand, Australia and Japan.

Edinburgh head coach Sean Everitt revealed Graham is facing at least 12 weeks on the sidelines as he recovers from a rupture. Describing the collision incident as "pretty freakish", Everitt, said: "That's not good news for us and not good news for him, especially with the autumn series coming up."

Tennis.title: GB's Kartal wins on WTA return after six months out
Tennis.summary: Britain's Sonay Kartal wins on her return to the WTA Tour after six months out with injury as she beats Andrea Lazaro Garcia at the China Open.
Tennis.body:
Britain's Sonay Kartal won on her return to the WTA Tour after almost six months out with injury as she beat Andrea Lazaro Garcia at the China Open. The 24-year-old injured her lower back at Indian Wells in March and only made her return to tennis at the Billie Jean King Cup on 22 September.

Kartal, who narrowly lost to Czech world number 26 Marie Bouzkova on that return last week, produced a confident performance in Beijing to beat Spain's Lazaro Garcia 6-2 6-3. The Briton broke the qualifier's serve five times - helped by four double faults from her opponent - and landed 69% of her first serves.

Tennis.title: 'I kept fighting right to the end'
Tennis.summary: A tearful Kei Nishikori says he "kept fighting right to the end" as the former world number four ends his professional career at the Japan Open.
Tennis.body:
A tearful Kei Nishikori said he "kept fighting right to the end" as the former world number four ended his professional career at the Japan Open. Nishikori, known as one of the best players to never win a Grand Slam, lost 6-4 6-4 to world number eight Frances Tiafoe in Tokyo.

The 36-year-old became the first Japanese man to reach a major final when he faced Marin Cilic in the 2014 US Open showpiece. Nishikori beat then world number one Novak Djokovic on his way to the New York final and defeated Rafael Nadal for Olympic bronze at the 2016 Games in Rio.

Tennis.title: Navarro opens up on health struggles that caused 'deep anger' on court
Tennis.summary: American Emma Navarro says she has gained her "life back" as she shares her long-running health problems that caused significant weight loss, fatigue, dizziness and left her "feeling deep internal anger" on the court.
Tennis.body:
American Emma Navarro says she has gained her "life back" after opening up on long-running health problems that caused significant weight loss, fatigue, dizziness and left her "feeling deep internal anger" on the court.

Navarro, who claimed her first title in more than a year at the Strasbourg Open in May, is currently ranked 24th in the world. The 25-year-old was as high as eighth in 2024, the year she reached the quarter-finals at the Australian Open and Wimbledon, and the last four at the US Open in her native New York.

Tennis.title: Djokovic wins first match since Wimbledon in China
Tennis.summary: Novak Djokovic beats Nuno Borges at the China Open to secure his first win since reaching the Wimbledon semi-finals in July.
Tennis.body:
Novak Djokovic maintained his remarkable unbeaten record at the China Open as he beat Nuno Borges to secure his first win since reaching the Wimbledon semi-finals in July. The 39-year-old former world number one struggled in the second set but came through to win 6-3 7-6 (7-2) for his 30th consecutive victory in Beijing, albeit in his first appearance at the event since 2015.

Djokovic revealed in August that he has been dealing with an underlying health condition that causes particular issues in hot, humid conditions for "the past couple of years" and was far from his best against Portuguese Borges.

Tennis.title: Emma Raducanu drops in rankings again after pulling out of another event
Tennis.summary: Emma Raducanu drops in rankings again after pulling out of another event AOL.com
Tennis.body:
Emma Raducanu has taken another hit in the rankings after withdrawing from the China Open due to a stress fracture in her right leg. The former US Open champion hasn't competed since making it to the Queen's Club final in June. The setback forced her to sit out Wimbledon and prevented a return to Flushing Meadows, where she made history with her Grand Slam victory in 2021.

Initially, Raducanu appeared on the entry list for the China Open, sparking optimism about her anticipated return in Beijing. Yet she was removed from the list weeks before the tennis event, suggesting her injury continues to linger. Her absence from competition has significantly impacted her WTA ranking, with the 23-year-old experiencing a dramatic decline.

Tennis.title: Andy Murray’s recent comments about Jack Draper are surely positive news for 2027
Tennis.summary: Andy Murray’s recent comments about Jack Draper are surely positive news for 2027 Tennishead
Tennis.body:
Jack Draper has suffered the toughest year of his career in 2026, just when many predicted it might be his best. After all, last season saw him truly break through and establish himself amongst the sport’s elite, winning his maiden Masters 1000 title before reaching the fourth round at Roland Garros.

However, it was around then when the fitness fears began, and after a tough Wimbledon campaign where he bowed out early, concerns only grew. The Brit had to withdraw from the US Open and shut down his season, and has spent most of 2026 doing the same. Draper recently announced he’d be ending this year early too, and will now look ahead to 2027.

Tennis.title: Andy Murray Reveals Jack Draper Plans as Ranking Drop Creates New Concern
Tennis.summary: Andy Murray Reveals Jack Draper Plans as Ranking Drop Creates New Concern Yardbarker
Tennis.body:
When Andy Murray and Jack Draper joined forces this year, British tennis had huge expectations from the team-up. However, given Draper’s injury woes, it would have been understandable if there was speculation about Murray staying on as the coach, given the fickle nature of coaching partnerships in tennis. However, the former World No.1 had a very firm and practical answer when asked the question about his role in Draper’s team for 2027.

“Yeah, there’s still plans to help him,” Murray said in a Sky Sports interview. “I don’t know where that is. I’m not entirely sure because his ranking will have dropped. I don’t know if he would get into Australia, and potentially relying on wild cards and things like that, so we’ll see. “Hopefully he’ll be back on the court training again soon and getting ready for the new season – it has been an interesting year.”

Tennis.title: Zverev comeback leads Europe to Laver Cup victory
Tennis.summary: Alexander Zverev recovers from his day two defeat by Alex de Minaur to beat Learner Tien and clinch the Laver Cup title for Team Europe on the final day.
Tennis.body:
Alexander Zverev beat Learner Tien on the final day of the Laver Cup to lead Team Europe to their sixth title. US Open champion Zverev recovered from a disappointing defeat by Team World's Alex de Minaur on day two and eased to a 7-6 (7-3) 6-3 win over Tien at London's O2 Arena.

Golf.title: Caolan Rafferty is Ireland's grand slam winner you don't know
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy won the career Grand Slam at Augusta in 2025. Six months later, amateur Caolan Rafferty became Ireland's other slam winner. The post Caolan Rafferty is Ireland’s grand slam winner you don’t know appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
In April of last year, Rory McIlroy crumpled to the ground at Augusta National, having finally won the Masters to complete the career Grand Slam. Six months later, the Isle of Ireland got another slam winner — one who has no equal. While McIlroy, who is from Northern Ireland, was the sixth member to join professional golf’s most prestigious club, Caolan Rafferty — who is from Dundalk, Ireland — is the only amateur ever to complete the “Provincial Slam” by winning the North, South, East, and West of Ireland championships.

The list of legendary Irish amateurs is long. The names include McIlroy, Shane Lowry, Darren Clarke, Padraig Harrington, J.B. Carr, John Burke and Hugh Foley, among others. And yet many of the biggest names didn’t have the extended amateur run that Rafferty has had, as they eventually turned to professional golf. Clarke and Foley won three of the four legs of the Provincial before turning pro. Lowry won two.

Golf.body:
Rory McIlroy will play the Abu Dhabi Championship at Yas Links from November 5 to 8, the DP World Tour has confirmed. The announcement came alongside news that Aldar, the Abu Dhabi real estate developer that owns the course, has become title partner of the first of the season’s two Play-Off events. The tournament will now be known as the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship.

McIlroy arrives as six-time major champion, the reigning Masters champion and the defending Race to Dubai champion. He has never won in Abu Dhabi. “I’ve finished runner-up here four times, so I’d obviously love to go one better and finally win it,” he said. “I really enjoy finishing my season in the UAE, and hopefully I can have a strong week and put myself in a position to win another Race to Dubai title.”

Golf.title: This psychedelic golf retreat is a trip in more ways than one
Golf.summary: Guests stay five nights at a luxe seaside home in Los Cabos with an expert ayahuasca practitioner on site around the clock. The post This psychedelic golf retreat is a trip in more ways than one appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Golf courses are full of hazards, but the game itself isn’t dangerous. It’s not high-speed like auto racing or high-impact like the NFL. While you might tweak your back or jam a wrist, the risk of lasting harm is vanishingly low.

So why, when you play, are you so often afraid? Christopher Smith has long wrestled with the question. A GOLF Top 100 Teacher who has been an instructor for more than 35 years, Smith knows that sound mechanics can calm the heebie-jeebies (it’s not a bad idea to take a lesson!), and that mental strength can be a salve (nothing wrong with seeing a sports psychologist!). But he believes getting to the source of fear and discomfort sometimes requires going deeper.

Golf.summary: As LIV Golf works through banktruptcy, loose ends from LIV 1.0 are already affecting the prospectus for LIV 2.0. The post LIV Golf’s future is battling its past, new bankruptcy filings reveal appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The next few weeks will decide much of LIV Golf’s future, as milestone dates for its deal with BC Partners are approaching. But recent filings open a window into how tense and tricky filing for bankruptcy can be.

Scotland's number one golfer, Robert MacIntyre, has called for Carnoustie and Muirfield to become regular venues again for the Open Championship. Carnoustie last hosted the tournament in 2018, when Italy's Francesco Molinari lifted the Claret Jug, while Muirfield's most recent staging was in 2013.

Next year's Open will be held at St Andrews and MacIntyre says more regular visits to Scotland would be a major boost for the game in the country. "That would be brilliant," he said. "I feel like there's not enough Open Championships in Scotland anymore.

Golf.title: Viktor Hovland's endless quest has him frustrated after 'pretty shocking' week in France
Golf.summary: Viktor Hovland hoped he was close to finding his old self, but one illuminating quote in France shows his endless quest continues to drag on. The post Viktor Hovland’s endless quest has him frustrated after ‘pretty shocking’ week in France appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Last month, Viktor Hovland’s PGA Tour season ended with a near-miss at the Tour Championship. It was a week that started with Hovland finding “something’ that allowed him to “hit the ball straight” to vault into contention at East Lake. Hovland was in position to win entering the final round but stalled, shooting 2-over as Scottie Scheffler caught and passed him to take the title.

Hovland has been in search mode for a while. He has won each of the past two seasons with the combination of a hot putter and a knack for competition, but that’s not what he’s looking for. He’s looking for something that is both familiar and foreign: who he used to be.

Golf.body:
For the average recreational golfer, the commonly cited odds of making a hole-in-one are approximately 12,500 to 1. For an albatross, or double eagle — a 2 on a par 5 — it’s approximately 6 million to 1.

Those odds are 1 in 14.5 quadrillion, according to one computation, which we’ll explain in a moment. In other words, virtually impossible. And yet — you guessed it — it happened.

Golf.title: Rules Guy: What's the maximum number of penalty strokes you can accrue on 1 shot?
Golf.summary: Is there a limit to the number of penalty strokes you can accrue by hitting a single tee shot? Rules Guy has the answer. The post Rules Guy: What’s the maximum number of penalty strokes you can accrue on 1 shot? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The Rules of Golf are tricky! Thankfully, we’ve got the guru. Our Rules Guy knows the book front to back. Got a question? He’s got all the answers. Hypothetical question: How many penalty strokes could a player get from hitting one tee shot? My thought: He’s late for his tee time, asks his opponent what club he used, tees it up in front of the marker, has too many clubs in his bag, uses an illegal club or ball, and then hits it out of bounds. Your thoughts? —Todd Sherstad, via email

First thought: Rules Guy needs more coffee to tackle this convoluted theoretical, but then sufficient caffeine kicked in. In 2023, Rule 1.3c(4) was designed to help limit the number of penalty strokes players could accumulate between strokes, so long as they were unaware of the breaches at the time. Thus, theoretically, absent that awareness, a player should only be able to rack up three penalty strokes in one shot — two for a breach and one for stroke and distance after hitting it out of bounds.

Golf.body:
Wherever there’s a lighthouse, it’s common to find a links nearby. No wonder, really. The same rugged shores that pose a risk to ships are often ideal grounds for golf. Take the South Ayrshire coast of Scotland, home to a fabled championship layout and one of the best-known beacons in the game.

A postcard staple for generations, and now a star of countless Instagram feeds, the Turnberry Lighthouse cuts a striking profile beside the 9th hole of Trump Turnberry, overlooking the Ailsa Course and the Firth of Clyde, with humpbacked Ailsa Craig rising like a half-moon on the horizon.

Golf.title: Above Par: Precedent for LIV Golf’s Bankruptcy
Golf.summary: Above Par: Precedent for LIV Golf’s Bankruptcy wislawjournal.com
Golf.body:
LIV Golf New Jersey LLC filed for Chapter 11 protection on September 8, 2026, in the District of New Jersey. Five billion dollars in capital from Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund funded five years of the tour before the money ran out. The rescue plan behind it comes with its own clock: BC Partners has agreed to anchor a $300 million recapitalization, but the restructuring support agreement gives LIV’s players 35 days from the petition date to sign on, or the deal is at risk. Player claims run to roughly $45 million, with Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau each owed more than $5 million of it.

None of this is unfamiliar to anyone who has spent time in sports bankruptcy dockets. We pulled fourteen professional sports cases filed over the last twenty years, from the New York Racing Association in 2006 to Grand Slam Track last December, and the range of outcomes across that set maps closely onto what LIV Golf is entering now.

Golf.title: How the Presidents Cup unraveled: 7 tipping points that cost the Internationals
Golf.summary: Something strange happened in the final seven singles matches at the Presidents Cup — and cost the Internationals the win. The post How the Presidents Cup unraveled: 7 tipping points that cost the Internationals appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
MEDINAH, Ill. — Something strange happened with the final seven Presidents Cup singles matches on Sunday: They all made it to at least the 17th hole. Heck, five of those made it all the way to 18.

But even though the matches were close, the outcomes weren’t: The United States team won those matches 6.5 to 0.5. And so they won the Presidents Cup. “It was sort of on a knife’s edge for a long time there in the middle of the day,” said International captain Geoff Ogilvy just after the Cup was clinched. “You have a couple putts go in at the right time and the momentum goes our way, and it just didn’t do that today.”

The Internationals had Team USA broken and their own miracle at Medinah in reach. But their Sunday collapse exposed the flaw the Presidents Cup can no longer ignore. The United States simply reached the Presidents Cup’s Sunday singles, stopped trying to play as a team and remembered that, as individuals, they were much better golfers.

Golf.body:
MEDINAH, Ill. — It was a sad scene: A group of golfers, dressed in black, milling about in silence. Their caddies and families, standing beside them. And all watching as their red-shirted counterparts spilled onto the 18th green at Medinah Country Club, the United States team celebrating a win the International team had desperately wanted for themselves.

A scene only made sadder because one of their teammates had already hit the road. Tom Kim had played his heart out. He’d earned four points for his squad — the most by any golfer on either side — and he’d stayed as long as he could. And then, when he ducked out early, it was for good reason.

Golf.title: Think you want to be Team USA captain? Think again
Golf.summary: American Presidents Cup or Ryder Cup captains sign up for a whole bunch of stress. We saw that with Brandt Snedeker. The post Think you want to be Team USA captain? Think again appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
MEDINAH, Ill. — Brandt Snedeker spent a sizable chunk of his Sunday evening pacing back and forth, back and forth between the 15th green and 16th tee. From afar, he looked steely, but up close, he was a frenzied mess of thoughts.

His phone was in and out of his pocket, one hand almost always covering his mouth, masking his words like a baseball pitcher does with his glove. He’d whisper softly into his radio set, then project more forcibly to his increasingly giddy American players, then back to a whisper for his assistant captains.

Golf.title: Grading every Presidents Cup performance from U.S. comeback at Medinah
Golf.summary: After another U.S. Presidents Cup win, let's grade every performance from a busy week for both sides at Medinah. The post Grading every Presidents Cup performance from U.S. comeback at Medinah appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
In the end, the 2026 Presidents Cup was an exercise in extremes. And in the end, American dominance in singles play outweighed its ineptitude in alternate shot. After several stressful, underwhelming days from the home team reignited years-long debates about American match play preparation and team strategy, a 9-2-1 performance on Sunday at Medinah reminded us that, in the end, the best way to win at team golf competitions is to have the best players. If there was any doubt before the competition began in Chicago, there is no doubt now: the Americans are the more talented side.

Every year, team play competitions are an opportunity for the sport to take stock of itself. Is the American crop of talent as good as it looks on paper? Has the golden generation of International talent aged into a formidable threat to American dominance? Who are the young stars that will come to define the next decade of the event?

Golf.body:
Brandt Snedeker admitted to making “mistakes” as Team USA fell behind at the Presidents Cup at Medinah. With the Internationals taking a three-point lead into Sunday, there was no denying Snedeker’s claim that he had erred several times, including benching Scottie Scheffler in foursomes and a questionable pairing. The Americans’ leader had put them in a tough spot.

But when the dust settled on Sunday night after the Americans stormed back to win the Presidents Cup with a singles barrage, one thing was clear: Snedeker’s biggest decision likely won the Americans the Presidents Cup. It was a choice he made a month ago, but the payoff came at a critical juncture in Team USA’s historic comeback.

On Sunday, the American team did what American teams always do when playing for cups of every size and shape, be it your Curtis Cup or Walker Cup, your Presidents Cup, your Solheim Cup, your Ryder Cup. Not always always, but pretty much always. Win or lose, when American golfers are playing their own ball in an 18-hole mano-a-mano match, they outplay their opponents.

In 1999, at the Ryder Cup at the Country Club near Boston, the Americans pulled out an unlikely victory with an 8.5-3.5 shellacking in the third and final act. Last year, at the Ryder Cup at Bethpage near New York, the Americans won another 8.5 points on Sunday, though that time it wasn’t enough to snatch victory from the mouth of defeat. On Sunday at Medinah at the Presidents Cup, the Americans won 9.5 points and the Internationals only 2.5 in a 17-13 American win.

Golf.title: US complete thrilling comeback to retain Presidents Cup
Golf.summary: The United States complete a thrilling comeback on the final day to beat the Internationals and win an 11th successive Presidents Cup.
Golf.body:
The United States completed a thrilling comeback on the final day to beat the Internationals and win an 11th successive Presidents Cup. The hosts, containing eight of the world's 11 top-ranked players, trailed by three points going into Sunday and were looking to avoid just a second defeat since the biennial competition began 32 years ago.

They dominated the singles, winning nine of the 12 matches, to seal a 17-13 win at Medinah - the scene of Team Europe's famous Ryder Cup comeback win in 2012. Jacob Bridgeman secured the decisive point by holing a four-foot par putt at the 18th to seal a one-up win over Australia's Min Woo Lee.

Golf.body:
U.S. captain Brandt Snedeker knows that no lead is safe around Medinah. Snedeker was on the U.S. Ryder Cup team that blew a 10-6 lead to the Europeans at the Chicago course in 2012.

So while Snedeker’s team entered Sunday at the 2026 Presidents Cup trailing the Internationals 10.5-7.5, he believed that things were far from over. That belief — in both his team and whatever Medinah mystique might exist — proved prophetic on Sunday as the Americans came out early in singles with a flurry of haymakers to grab the momentum and put the pressure on the underdog Internationals before polishing off a Sunday comeback, the biggest in Presidents Cup history.

Golf.summary: How this week’s Presidents Cup has dealt yet another blow to LIV Golf’s survival hopes Yahoo Sports
Golf.body:
Whatever happens on Sunday at Medinah, this year's Presidents Cup has unquestionably been a triumph that the event desperately needed. The International Team went into the singles with their first ever lead on American soil. There is no question that Geoff Ogilvy has completely outshone Brandt Snedeker, and given his side a phenomenal opportunity to secure their first victory since 1998.

The Internationals have certainly silenced those of us who had awarded the trophy to Team USA before a single shot had been hit this week. And with that, it is perhaps fair to say that this year's Presidents Cup has dealt yet another blow to LIV Golf by proving that those who made the jump are not needed.

Golf.title: What players and captains earn at the Presidents Cup
Golf.summary: At the Presidents Cup, performance has no bearing on payout, but the winning team walks off with a golden prize. The post What players and captains earn at the Presidents Cup appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
There was a time when playing for pride and country was enough. At its birth in 1994, the Presidents Cup paid its competitors exactly nothing. Every dollar the event generated went to charity. For 13 editions, from 1994 through 2021, no player, captain or vice captain received a cent personally. The Tour allocated money in their names to charities of their choosing instead.

That changed in 2022, when the PGA Tour introduced a $250,000 stipend for participants to use at their own discretion. The money is no longer earmarked for charity, though many players and captains still choose to give it all away. The Tour also continues to guarantee at least $1 million in charitable impact for the host city.

Golf.title: The next two Presidents Cups? Here's where they'll be held
Golf.summary: The next two editions of the Presidents Cup will bring the biennial competition to courses that have never staged the event. The post The next two Presidents Cups? Here’s where they’ll be held appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
In the beginning, the Presidents Cup pressed repeat. For its first two editions, in 1994 and 1996, the Ryder Cup-style competition pitting the United States against the world (minus the UK, Ireland and continental Europe) was played at the same course: Robert Trent Jones Golf Club, in Gainesville, VA, a venue chosen largely for its proximity to the nation’s capital. The event, after all, was called the Presidents Cup, with Gerald Ford as its honorary chairman. It made sense to keep things close to Washington, D.C.

In those early goings, the PGA Tour, which created the event, had no plans to take it overseas at all. Not until it had gathered momentum — with the stirrings of a fan base and sponsor interest — did the competition settle into its current rhythm, shifting back and forth, every two years, between the U.S. and overseas (it was postponed in 2001 by the attacks of Sept. 11, and then again in 2020 by the pandemic). In 1998, the biennial battle moved to Australia; Royal Melbourne Golf Club was the stage.

Golf.title: 'Disaster': Jack Sock describes experience playing PGA National on PRO Tour
Golf.summary: On this week's Subpar, tennis pro Jack Sock described what it was like to play against other pro athletes at PGA National in 35 mph winds. The post ‘Disaster’: Jack Sock describes experience playing PGA National on PRO Tour appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
What do high-achieving pro athletes do to keep their competitive juices flowing after they’ve retired from their respective sports? Many take up golf, and some even showcase their skills on the celebrity pro-am circuit. But for a select few who desire even higher stakes, there’s the PRO Tour — an invitation-based tournament series created specifically for former pro athletes. The criteria for consideration: A player must have a minimum of two years of professional playing experience in their sport, a verified single-digit golf handicap, and a demonstrated commitment to preparation, professionalism, and competition.

Interested athletes can apply on the tour’s website to be considered to participate. In its inaugural season, the PRO Tour staged six regular-season events followed by two playoff events. Each event had a $500,000 purse. Top finishers in each event earn priority placement in subsequent events, while new additions to the tour are rotated in over the course of the season. The PRO Tour utilizes a modified Stableford scoring system, in which players earn positive or negative points on each hole based on their score. The player with the highest number of points over the course of the tournament wins.

Golf.title: Can the U.S. make a Sunday comeback to avoid Presidents Cup upset?
Golf.summary: The Internationals lead heading into Sunday at the Presidents Cup. Can the Americans mount a comeback to avoid a historic upset? The post Can the U.S. make a Sunday comeback to avoid Presidents Cup upset? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
After failing to take advantage of a golden opportunity to trim the Internationals’ lead on Saturday, Team USA will enter Sunday at the Presidents Cup trailing 10.5-7.5. It’s the first time in Presidents Cup history that the International team has led entering Sunday on U.S. soil. There will be 12 points up for grabs on Sunday. Will the Americans mount a comeback, or will the International team finish off a historic upset?

Josh Berhow, managing editor: The Americans might still be the betting favorites — singles is where their superior depth really shines — but let’s get crazy and say the Internationals finally pull off the upset. Back in 2017, this event was over before the weekend; two years after that, the Americans held a two-point lead into the weekend, and in the last two events, the U.S. has led 11-7 heading into singles. Now, with the Internationals finally in front heading into Sunday (10.5-7.5), I think it’s just enough cushion to not only give them a bit of a head start but the confidence they need to realize they can actually do it. And if they do win? Then the Presidents Cup finally gets some much-needed juice.

Golf.title: ‘We need a few more answers’: Why Cameron Smith’s future on LIV tour is still uncertain
Golf.summary: ‘We need a few more answers’: Why Cameron Smith’s future on LIV tour is still uncertain SMH.com.au
Golf.body:
Cameron Smith answers the phone from Versailles, where the Australian golfer is contesting the French Open on the European Tour. “Bonjour,” he says, breaking into laughter. The 2022 British Open champion joined former US Open winner Matt Fitzpatrick and Tommy Fleetwood this week at Le Golf National, an hour from Paris. Smith was a late and surprise addition to make his event debut.

“Mate, I had never even been to France before this week,” Smith said. It’s among a handful of late-year events to help Smith stay competitive until December, when he hopes to win a maiden Australian Open crown after two second places, including a crushing, final-hole bogey at Royal Melbourne last year.

Golf.summary: The Internationals team could secure a first President's Cup in 28 years on Sunday after holding off a United States fightback on day three in Medinah.
Golf.body:
The International team need five points on the final day to secure a first Presidents Cup in 28 years after holding off a United States fightback on day three in Medinah. The Internationals were behind in every match at one stage but will go into Sunday's singles holding a 10-5-7.5 lead.

Golf.title: Internationals' lead is first of its kind in Presidents Cup history
Golf.summary: The International team made Presidents Cup history on Saturday after the U.S. let a golden opportunity slip through its fingers. The post Internationals’ lead is first of its kind in Presidents Cup history appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
For a large part of Saturday, it looked like U.S. captain Brandt Snedeker would prove prophetic. After the Americans were swept in Friday’s foursomes session by the Internationals, Snedeker said he wasn’t concerned that the U.S. was about to lose its first Presidents Cup in almost 30 years.

“This thing is 35, 40 percent over — it’s not even halftime of a football game,” Snedeker said on Friday as the Internationals took a 7-3 lead. “There’s a lot of golf left.” The Americans chipped away at the Internationals’ lead early on Saturday, winning the morning’s fourball session 2.5-1.5. Then came Saturday’s foursomes session, a format the Americans have struggled in of late, going 6-24 in alternate-shot sessions in team competitions since 2023.

Golf.title: U.S. benches Scottie Scheffler in controversial foursomes move, captain responds
Golf.summary: Scottie Scheffler was benched on Saturday afternoon at the Presidents Cup in a "really tough decision" by U.S. captain Brandt Snedeker. The post U.S. benches Scottie Scheffler in controversial foursomes move, captain responds appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
It was strange seeing Scottie Scheffler on the first tee Saturday afternoon at the Presidents Cup — because his shirt was untucked, he’d cracked open a bag of chips and was laughing off to the side with a group of U.S. family members and support staff.

It must have been strange for Scheffler, too. That’s because, for the first time in three years, he was sitting out a session in U.S. team competition. With the Internationals leading the U.S. team 8.5-5.5 heading into Saturday afternoon’s foursomes sessions, captain Brandt Snedeker put out a lineup that he said included “a couple wrinkles.” One of those was splitting up the Scheffler-Sam Burns pairing, which went 2-1 over the first three sessions.

TOMS RIVER, N.J., Sept. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire-PRWeb/ -- New Jersey bankruptcy law firm Straffi & Straffi Attorneys at Law is seeking to speak with individuals, businesses, vendors, contractors, service providers, players, and employees who believe LIV Golf LLC owes them money following the league's Chapter 11 bankruptcy filing in New Jersey.

LIV Golf filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of New Jersey on September 8, 2026. The filing reports estimated assets of $100 million to $500 million and estimated liabilities of $500 million to $1 billion. Bankruptcy documents list several high-profile golfers among the creditors, including Jon Rahm, Bryson DeChambeau, and Cameron Smith.

Golf.title: 5 keys for clearing a high lip out of the bunker
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Kellie Stenzel shares five keys for clearing a high lip from. a deep greenside bunker. The post 5 keys for clearing a high lip out of the bunker appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Why do great golfers seem to have no trouble with a deep bunker and a high lip, while it strikes fear into so many others? The answer isn’t talent so much as technique. Once you understand a few key principles, clearing even the most intimidating lip becomes much more manageable.

Here are five keys for getting out of a deep greenside bunker. A lob wedge (60°), sand wedge (56°) or gap wedge (50°) has enough loft to clear all but the most extreme lips. These clubs are designed with plenty of loft and bounce — the rounded sole that allows the club to glide through the sand rather than dig into it. Trust that the loft is doing its job; your motion simply needs to let it work.

Golf.summary: Watch: U.S. golf star chuckles at Bryson DeChambeau dig during Presidents Cup golfmagic.com
Golf.body:
Bryson DeChambeau was not at Medinah for the opening day of the Presidents Cup, but the two-time U.S. Open champion still managed to make an appearance of sorts. A spectator watching Sam Burns during Thursday's opening matches invoked DeChambeau while Burns prepared to play a shot from the rough, drawing a laugh from the American.

"The grass was standing up, but I DeChambeau'd it for you," the fan said. The comment was a reference to the two-stroke penalty DeChambeau received during this year's Open Championship at Royal Birkdale after officials ruled that he had improved the lie of his ball by stepping on grass surrounding it..

Golf.title: He traded golf for ‘American Ninja Warrior.’ The game pulled him back
Golf.summary: Few U.S. Mid-Amateur qualifiers have taken more circuitous, or adventurous, routes to their first Mid-Am starts than Nathaniel Spencer. The post He traded golf for ‘American Ninja Warrior.’ The game pulled him back appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
When Nathaniel Spencer, who now is 41, was a high-school golfer at the chock-full-o-athletes IMG Academy in Bradenton, Fla., he talked his way into playing center-back in a scrimmage with the school’s supremely talented soccer team. Among the standouts on the field was Freddy Adu, an attacking midfielder who, at 14, had become the youngest athlete ever to sign a professional contract in the United States when he came to terms with the Major League Soccer team, D.C. United.

Spencer, who had played competetive soccer growing up but only at the local level, said he didn’t know who Adu was; he also didn’t care to know. He wanted only to shut Adu down, and shut him down he did, Spencer said. So suffocating was Spencer’s defense, he said, that the coaches inquired about his interest in joining the team.

Golf.title: American said Presidents Cup vibe was 'dead.' So here's 1 humble proposal
Golf.summary: American Wyndham Clark said the Presidents Cup vibe was “dead.” And now the U.S. is down 7-3. So here’s one humble proposal. The post American said Presidents Cup vibe was ‘dead.’ So here’s 1 humble proposal appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
MEDINAH, Ill. — Wyndham Clark wanted noise, and he knew how that sounded. “These guys are going to laugh,” Clark said, motioning to Scottie Scheffler and Sam Burns sitting next to him.

Clark, after all, had heard unpleasantries this year, even while winning the U.S. Open, which, by every account, should be a pleasant moment. There’d even been whispers that he was a villain, which here, in the Chicago area, is a term reserved for those who ask for a thin slice. But Thursday night, after Clark and partner Collin Morikawa won their Day 1 four-balls match at the Presidents Cup, Clark gave us the definition of irony.
Golf.copy:
MEDINAH, Ill. — Wyndham Clark wanted noise, and he knew how that sounded. “These guys are going to laugh,” Clark said, motioning to Scottie Scheffler and Sam Burns sitting next to him.

Clark, after all, had heard unpleasantries this year, even while winning the U.S. Open, which, by every account, should be a pleasant moment. There’d even been whispers that he was a villain, which here, in the Chicago area, is a term reserved for those who ask for a thin slice. But Thursday night, after Clark and partner Collin Morikawa won their Day 1 four-balls match at the Presidents Cup, Clark gave us the definition of irony.

Golf.title: Nick Taylor waited forever for his Presidents Cup moment. Then he delivered
Golf.summary: Nick Taylor has been waiting years for a shot at the Presidents Cup. Then it all arrived suddenly Friday afternoon. Here's what happened. The post Nick Taylor waited forever for his Presidents Cup moment. Then he delivered appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
MEDINAH, Ill. — Of all the roads to this Presidents Cup, Nick Taylor has traveled the longest. The 38-year-old Canadian has been on the cusp of this event for most of the past decade, never quite cracking the team. He’s won an impressive five times on the PGA Tour — more than almost all his teammates — but only once during a Presidents Cup year. It happened at the 2024 Phoenix Open, in February, a full six months before the International team was finalized, where he was left on the outside looking in. Earlier this week, he explained to GOLF.com how the pain of missing the ’24 Cup — held in his homeland — had subsided into acceptance. But then he watched from afar as his best friends competed in Canada and the scab got reopened all over again.

Finally now, in a year when he didn’t win, he got the positive phone call that he’d earned a spot. And then, on Wednesday evening, he was told by the same captain, Geoff Ogilvy, that he’d have to wait a bit longer — he had to sit the first session.

Golf.title: How did things go so wrong for U.S Presidents Cup team Friday?
Golf.summary: The International team swept Friday foursomes at the Presidents Cup to take a 7-3 lead heading into the weekend. How did they do it? The post How did things go so wrong for U.S Presidents Cup team Friday? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
It happened again: The International team swept Friday foursomes for the second straight Presidents Cup, although this time it gives them a 7-3 lead heading into the weekend at Medinah Country Club. How in the world did things go so wrong for the U.S. team?

Sean Zak, senior writer: Anyone who has watched American team golf over the last five years has seen this happen a few times now. It starts slowly, just a drip of a hole here, a hole there, and then suddenly it’s a flood of yellow. (Or blue.) I think there’s some anxiousness that creeps in for the Americans during this event, in particular, when they’re considered such favorites. You hate to simplify it to Internationals putting better, but that’s how a lot of holes were won: made 10- to 20-footers from the boys in yellow. It can flip real quick back in the other direction.

The International team produced a brilliant fightback in the foursomes on day two of the Presidents Cup to take a 7-3 lead over the United States. Golf.title: Caddie who quit mid-round on PGA Tour pro shares dust-up details
Golf.summary: What sparked the disagreement that made Alejandro Tosti's caddie Cliff Ellis quit mid-round? Ellis shared his side of the story. The post Caddie who quit mid-round on PGA Tour pro shares dust-up details appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Last week, PGA Tour player Alejandro Tosti and his caddie, Cliff Ellis, made headlines when Ellis removed his bib and abandoned Tosti’s bag in the 18th fairway — halfway through the pair’s round at the Cliffs at Walnut Cove, host of the Biltmore Championship Asheville.

Golf Channel cameras captured Tosti and Ellis having what appeared to be a brief but animated interaction just short of the 18th green right before Ellis walked off. Tosti continued his walk to the green and reportedly employed a fan from the gallery to carry his bag for the nine holes that remained in his first round. Tosti ultimately fired a 72, followed by a 71 in the second round with a new caddie, to miss the cut.

Golf.title: U.S. trails Presidents Cup after Internationals' shocking sweep
Golf.summary: The Internationals stunned the Americans with a 5-0 session sweep at the Presidents Cup on Friday and head into the weekend with a rare lead. The post U.S. trails Presidents Cup after Internationals’ shocking sweep appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Maybe they won’t admit it, but on Friday at the Presidents Cup, the Americans had to be thinking, if only for a moment, surely what happened two years ago couldn’t happen again.

When the underdog Internationals erased a 5-0 deficit to win all five foursomes matches on Day 2 of the 2024 Presidents Cup, it was a stunner. It also, ultimately, didn’t matter — the Americans cruised to their 10th straight win anyway — but it was a shockingly unnerving development for the Americans, who of course did not want to endure that same feeling today.

Golf.title: Why you keep thinning your fairway woods—and how to fix it
Golf.summary: Learn why you thin your fairway woods and how to fix it with a few simple setup and swing keys from GOLF Top 100 Teacher Debbie Doniger. The post Why you keep thinning your fairway woods—and how to fix it appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
If you regularly catch fairway woods thin, your instinct might be to blame your impact and try to manufacture more height—lifting the ball, trying to “get under it” or even making a steeper swing. But GOLF Top 100 Teacher Debbie Doniger says the better place to start is much earlier in the sequence: your setup.

One of the most common mistakes is positioning the ball too far forward. Many amateurs move it toward their lead foot because they assume a fairway wood should be struck on the upswing, like a driver.
