Golf.title: Intentionally or not, Ryder Cup prep is underway at this Presidents Cup
Golf.summary: U.S. captain Brandt Snedeker would never admit it, but his decisions appear to have Ryder Cup intentionality to them. That's a good thing. The post Intentionally or not, Ryder Cup prep is underway at this Presidents Cup appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
MEDINAH, Ill. — The imbalance of results for Team USA in its biggest team golf matches has driven us to this point: where the Americans winning the Presidents Cup feels like a formality, but winning the Ryder Cup feels harder than free-soloing El Capitan.

Disagree? My colleague Nick Piastowski asked U.S. players to explain the difference, and most seemed stumped. The two events are run by different organizations but are similar enough in theory that there should be connective tissue. And here, at Medinah, there’s more of it than ever before. In the literal sense, there’s the fact that the last home loss in either event, before last year’s Ryder Cup at Bethpage Black, came at Medinah in 2012. Three of the American captains this week — Keegan Bradley, Jim Furyk and Webb Simpson — were on that losing U.S. team.

Golf.summary: One rules move has the pros' full attention at the Presidents Cup at Medinah Country Club. Said one pro: "I've never seen anything like it." The post ‘Never seen anything like it’: Penal tactic has pros’ attention at Presidents Cup appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
MEDINAH, Ill. — Min Woo Lee says he looked out in front of him, then almost immediately looked for Geoff Ogilvy. A three-foot-tall, wooden, split-rail fence was buried into the ground just a few yards off the fairway down the entire left side of the first hole at this week’s Presidents Cup.

Was that … ? Nah, it couldn’t be. Ogilvy captains the International team that Lee is playing for at the Cup, and it felt counterproductive that the Medinah Country Club redesign, done by Ogilvy’s design team, would include shaking-in-your-golf-shoes out of bounds right out of the chute.

Golf.title: Here's what we learned on Day 1 of the Presidents Cup
Golf.summary: The U.S. grabbed an early lead in the 2026 Presidents Cup. What did we learn in Thursday's opening session? Our staffers chime in. The post Here’s what we learned on Day 1 of the Presidents Cup appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Scottie Scheffler and Sam Burns held on for a late point and the Americans grabbed a 3-2 lead over the underdog International squad on the opening day of the Presidents Cup at Medinah Country Club on Thursday. What did you learn on Day 1?

Josh Berhow, managing editor: I’m not sure I learned this but Min Woo Lee and Sungjae Im reiterated the fact that the Americans are deep and the Internationals cannot afford to lose close matches in which they have a chance. Scheffler and Burns played well early but gave Lee and Im several chances to steal that match and jolt a little energy down their lineup. But they couldn’t make enough birdies late and now their team goes into Day 2 trailing, although down 3-2 isn’t a bad spot for them in general. And if you want another example of the Americans’ depth, Jacob Bridgeman didn’t play Thursday but makes his Presidents Cup debut on Friday. He won on the PGA Tour four days ago.

Golf.title: Scheffler, Burns avoid upset as U.S. takes early Presidents Cup lead
Golf.summary: Scottie Scheffler and Sam Burns held on to earn a late point as the Americans grabbed a slim lead on Day 1 of the Presidents Cup. The post Scheffler, Burns avoid upset as U.S. takes early Presidents Cup lead appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The Internationals had a chance to take Day 1 of the Presidents Cup but Sungjae Im and Min Woo Lee weren’t able to flip the first match of the day. World No. 1 Scottie Scheffler and No. 8 Sam Burns beat that duo 1 up in the only match that went to the 18th hole at Medinah Country Club in four-ball play on Thursday in the Chicago suburbs.

The U.S. leads the four-day event 3-2, with five more points up for grabs in foursomes play (alternate shot) on Friday. “I saw a lot of good golf out there — 2-3 their way is not too bad,” said International team captain Geoff Ogilvy. “We had a couple of really good solid matches there, and we had a match go up to 18, which would have been nice if it went the other way, but 2-3, we’ll take that. The boys have got a round under their belt now.”

Golf.title: Beyond the golf: 5 surprising attractions at GOLF's Top 100 Resorts

Golf.body:
At the finest golf resorts, great courses, first-rate food and comfy accommodations are pretty much given. Beyond that, you might find a spa, a golf academy, a kids’ camp and enough outdoor pursuits, from fly fishing to falconry, to keep you busy from dawn to dusk. And then there are the things you never saw coming: a museum of exotic Americana, a walk through a labyrinth, a tree older than most civilizations, a cave beneath the golf course or a game drive in search of the Big Five. Here are five of our favorite quirky offerings from GOLF’s new Top 100 Resorts list.

Johnny Morris built Big Cedar as an homage to the Ozarks, where he was born and raised. The result is a resort that celebrates the great outdoors. But Morris didn’t forget the indoors, either. Among the musts at Big Cedar is the Ancient Ozarks Natural History Museum, Morris’s astounding personal collection, which ranges from arrowheads and dinosaur fossils to Sitting Bull’s war vest. You can even get a look at a lock of Abraham Lincoln’s hair.

Golf.title: The Solheim Cup's bewildering TV ratings elude easy answers
Golf.summary: The Solheim Cup's precipitous drop in U.S. TV viewership received an impassioned response from one competitor, but not an easy answer. The post The Solheim Cup’s bewildering TV ratings elude easy answers appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
“I don’t know what the f— we’re doing so wrong.” Those words belonged to Solheim Cup assistant captain Mel Reid, in a recent interview with Golf Channel’s Kira K. Dixon — and they were addressing a concerning trend. The Solheim Cup’s 2026 television ratings in the United States were nearly half of what they’d been for the last European Solheim Cup, just three years earlier.

Reid’ comments, which appeared on the pair’s Quiet Please! podcast, underscored the bigger issue facing the Solheim Cup, and women’s golf more broadly: Without TV support, the sport cannot hope to continue growing its revenues, and without bigger revenues, the sport cannot continue to grow at the rate that it would like to.
Golf.copy:

Golf.summary: Jon Rahm leaves LIV future open as Bryson DeChambeau takes a different path Yahoo Sports
Golf.body:
Jon Rahm's future with LIV Golf remains unsettled after the league entered bankruptcy protection and began reshaping its plans for 2027. Rahm has said he is willing to honor his existing LIV 1.0 contract, but he has not committed to the proposed new structure. Bryson DeChambeau has taken a different public approach.

His "I'm coming home" tease appeared to signal a major career move before his announcement centered on a new golf entertainment project. The contrasting messages have added another layer to LIV's uncertain next chapter. Both major champions remain tied to the league, while Rahm has publicly left his 2027 position open and DeChambeau has used his recent public messaging to promote a separate content project.

Golf.title: Fred Couples had a hunch. For U.S., it resulted in something special
Golf.summary: At the Presidents Cup on Wednesday, Xander Schauffele and Patrick Cantlay explained Fred Couples’ role in their team-event partnership. The post Fred Couples had a hunch. For U.S., it resulted in something special appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
One of the first times Xander Schauffele and Patrick Cantlay spent quality time together was over an intense game of gin rummy en route to the 2019 Presidents Cup in Australia. The U.S. team’s 26-hour charter from the Bahamas to Melbourne afforded the Presidents Cup rookies plenty of time to bond, and bond Schauffele and Cantlay did — over sets, runs and exchanging of dollars. The spark between the two players did not escape U.S. team vice-captain Fred Couples.

In Schauffele and Cantlay, Couples saw more than just budding pals — he saw a budding partnership. “Freddy [was] like, ‘Hey, I think these two guys would be unbelievable together,’” Schauffele said Wednesday from this year’s Presidents Cup at Medinah Country Club outside Chicago. “The way they play, they almost turn into one person when they’re playing alternate shot, which is all you can sort of ask for. And then just the way we interact. Holding each other accountable, but knowing that each of us are trying our absolute hardest on every shot. Just having each other’s back. Freddy sort of orchestrated that, and he was right.”

Golf.title: How to easily execute a longer greenside bunker shot
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Sarah Stone explains the keys to executing a long greenside bunker shot just like the pros do. The post How to easily execute a longer greenside bunker shot appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
With the Presidents Cup coming to Medinah Country Club and the recent redesign of the greenside bunkering, we’re likely to see the world’s best players faced with longer, more challenging bunker shots. Most golfers have an easier time mastering a short bunker shot 10-15 yards from the pin, but struggle when they are faced with a longer bunker shot.

The good news is that these longer bunker shots don’t have to be complicated. You generally have enough distance to launch the ball with some carry without having to hit a high, soft shot like you would on a shorter bunker shot.

Golf.title: 'Media has made me out to be villain': Major champ hopes to avoid hecklers at Presidents Cup
Golf.summary: Fans rooted against Wyndham Clark during his 2026 U.S. Open win. Now he's hoping the U.S. fans have his back at the 2026 Presidents Cup. The post ‘Media has made me out to be villain’: Major champ hopes to avoid hecklers at Presidents Cup appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Will the Chicago golf fans be kinder to Wyndham Clark than the Long Island fans were to him in June? That’s one question on the mind of the two-time major champion as the 2026 Presidents Cup gets underway at Medinah.

This summer, Clark fought through final-round struggles to win the 2026 U.S. Open at Shinnecock Hills. But he didn’t just fight his game in the final round. He also had to contend with unruly fans, many of whom were openly rooting against him as he battled for his second victory in America’s national championship.

Badminton.title: World Juniors: Africa Beckons
Badminton.summary: World Juniors: Africa Beckons BWF
Badminton.body:
When the VICTOR BWF World Junior Championships begin in Egypt on Monday 5 October, it will mark only the second time ever that the tournament has visited Africa. It has been 24 years since Pretoria in South Africa hosted the world’s premier junior tournament. With the 26th edition of the World Juniors, badminton in Africa is poised to make a big leap, entering new territory as it were. Participation from the continent is at a high – nine countries have entered.

Of the 47 teams competing at the BWF World Junior Team Championships for the Suhandinata Cup, 19 from Europe, 13 from Asia, four from Pan Am, and two from Oceania, besides nine from Africa.

Badminton.title: Asian Games: Vitidsarn, An Reign Supreme
Badminton.summary: Asian Games: Vitidsarn, An Reign Supreme BWF
Badminton.body:
Kunlavut Vitidsarn celebrated his return to the top of the world rankings by defeating Loh Kean Yew 21-12 21-16 for the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games gold medal on Tuesday. Both players had already made history by becoming their countries’ first men’s singles finalists. But Vitidsarn went one step further, denying Loh the rare feat of defeating two top-ranked players after the Singaporean had beaten Jonatan Christie in the quarterfinals.

“Really happy because I didn’t come here thinking about a medal. My (recent) performances haven’t been good enough,” admitted Vitidsarn. “Being world No.1 brings a lot of pressure because everyone thinks, ‘You are No. 1, how could you lose like this?’ It’s very difficult.”

Indonesia led a landmark day at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games, with two of their doubles pairs toppling the leading seeds while a string of firsts emerged in the singles draws.

Amri Syahnawi/Nita Violina Marwah produced an emphatic upset by dispatching top seeds Feng Yan Zhe/Huang Dong Ping 21-12 21-14 to reach the mixed doubles final. The victory carried extra weight as the Indonesians were denied by the Chinese pair in a close World Championships semifinal in August, and had lost all five of their previous meetings.

Badminton.title: Why Property-Linked Investments Connect Financials Blackwall (ASX:BWF) and CVC (ASX:CVC) Beyond the S&P/ASX 200
Badminton.summary: Why Property-Linked Investments Connect Financials Blackwall (ASX:BWF) and CVC (ASX:CVC) Beyond the S&P/ASX 200 kalkine.com.au
Badminton.body:
BlackWall (ASX:BWF) has no borrowings on its own balance sheet. CVC (ASX:CVC) ended June 2026 with A$224.8 million of them. Yet both companies make their money from the same underlying source: stakes in Australian property that they own alongside other investors rather than outright.

That shared model is what connects them. Neither is a real estate Investment trust, and both earn returns through investment stakes, but those returns depend on property values, rezoning, rents and asset sales. Looking at where each one's Leverage sits, and what it is trying to do next, shows how differently two small property-linked investors can be built.

Badminton.summary: Asian Games: Yoo Tae Bin’s Dream Run Continues BWF
Badminton.body:
Yoo Tae Bin’s breakthrough season continued to unfold as the world No.46 beat World Championships silver medallist Kodai Naraoka to make the semifinals of the Asian Games individual event.

The Korean, who was outside the top 100 a year ago, has had impressive results in recent months. Having beaten Lee Cheuk Yiu in the team event last week, Yoo created the sensation of the individual event beating Shi Yu Qi 21-17 25-23 in the Round of 16 yesterday, and followed up with a win over another top 10 player, Kodai Naraoka.

Badminton.title: Asian Games: Li Shi Feng Bites the Dust
Badminton.summary: Asian Games: Li Shi Feng Bites the Dust BWF
Badminton.body:
The Asian Games individual event saw yet another defending champion bow out early. Following the upset of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy/Chirag Shetty yesterday, it was men’s singles defending champion Li Shi Feng’s turn to head for the exit door. The seventh seed was beaten by Choi Ji Hoon, a player ranked 77 places below him, in a Round of 32 encounter that was close all the way: 18-21 21-19 21-18.

Among other significant results in the Round of 32 was the upset of All England champion Lin Chun-Yi to No.46 Yoo Tae Bin, with the Korean winning 21-10 21-12. In another well-fought match in the same round, Loh Kean Yew battled past eighth seed Lakshya Sen in three games, and then eased past Justin Hoh to make the quarterfinals.

Badminton.body:
A couple of days after leading India to a bronze medal finish in the men’s team event of the Asian Games, defending champions Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty were stunned in the opening round of the individual event.

The world No.5 duo started well against world No.36 Peeratchai Sukphun/Pakkapon Teeraratsakul, taking the first game, but the Thais kept a narrow lead through most of the second and then steadily gained on the Indians to record a massive upset at 12-21 21-19 21-14.

Badminton.title: Asian Games: Indonesia Break Gold Medal Drought
Badminton.summary: Asian Games: Indonesia Break Gold Medal Drought BWF
Badminton.body:
Indonesia staged a magnificent comeback to beat China for the men’s team gold at the Asian Games, breaking a drought that has stretched over two decades. Last victorious in 1998, Indonesia pulled off the come-from-behind victory having fallen 0-2 behind. Jonatan Christie had fallen to Shi Yu Qi in the opening match, and then Fajar Alfian/Muhammad Shohibul Fikri were outplayed in three games by world champions Liang Wei Keng/Wang Chang.

It was youngster Alwi Farhan who turned things around, as he prevailed in a match of fluctuating fortunes that lasted 87 minutes against Li Shi Feng. Farhan pulled through 23-21 15-21 21-16 to keep Indonesia in the hunt.

Competitor News.title: Standard Chartered turns F1 strategy into a brand story
Competitor News.summary: Standard Chartered turns F1 strategy into a brand story ContentGrip
Competitor News.body:
Standard Chartered has moved its Formula 1 partnership from sponsorship asset to brand story. Its new global campaign, "Move Ahead", does not focus only on speed, cars or race-day spectacle. Instead, the bank uses the preparation behind Formula 1 as a metaphor for how clients make decisions, manage risk and move across markets.

That distinction matters for marketers. Sports sponsorships often stop at access, logos and hospitality. Standard Chartered is trying to turn the behavior of the sport itself into a way to explain what the brand does.

Competitor News.title: Mayor Fillmore pursuing DND partnership for arena to replace Halifax Forum
Competitor News.summary: Mayor Fillmore pursuing DND partnership for arena to replace Halifax Forum CTV News
Competitor News.body:
Approaching its 100th birthday, an age-old debate about what to do with the Halifax Forum is once again heating up. It’s set for a rebuild at the same location, for a ballooned cost of $126 million.

But late Friday afternoon, the city posted on social media saying staff have decided to pause the demolition application because costs have gone higher than what was planned for – but the city’s not yet saying how far over budget.
